name: Albino Tom Tom
description: Its wide melee attacks have knockback 2.
attackStyle: Melee attack, Hits the immediate 3 front tiles Knockback 2
wikiBehavior:
* Uses a wide melee attack, similar to a Tom Tom, with knockback 2. 
* Prioritizes launching [[obj:Boulder]] if possible.
wikiTrivia:
* Its name is the first alphabetically out of any enemy in the game.
* Its appearance is similar to the rare bad outcome of the event encountered in [[chapter:The Jurassic]], which give the player’s cat the disorder [[disorder:Albinism]] and the a mutation.
* Their pale appearance is suggestive of [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troglomorphism|troglomorphism]], meaning it has common traits associated with animals that live in constant darkness.

name: Amoeba
description: Can attach itself to equipment slots on cats, and will break existing equipment if it does. Will attempt to find a rock to defend itself.
wikiBehavior:
The Amoeba prioritizes picking up any [[type:Rock]] unit, such as [[obj:Small Rock]], [[obj:Boulder]],  Rock Head or [[status:Petrify]] units to use as protection.  After picking up such a unit, the amoeba will gain [[status:Shield]] equal to the health of the rock, and its melee attack will deal that amount of damage as well. When killed in this state, it drops the unit it was holding with harming it.

When no rocks are available, amoebas will instead directly attack cats. When this attack connects, it forcibly equips a [[status:Cursed]] amoeba armor item (either [[item:Amoeba (Face)]], [[item:Amoeba (Head)]], or [[item:Amoeba (Neck)]]) to the cat, destroying whatever was in the chosen slot beforehand.
wikiTrivia:
* An  Amoeba is a type of cell or unicellular organism with the ability to alter its shape, primarily by extending and retracting pseudopods.
* The amoeba’s appearance and parasitic nature may be a reference to the [[url:https://theinfosphere.org/Brain_slugs|Brain Slugs]] from Futurama.

name: Angelic Cat
description: Has a Holy Wind area attack. Gains 1 Holy Shield at the end of its turn. Immune to Holy. Gains All Stats Up when struck with Holy Element.
wikiBehavior:
Attacks with a T-shaped attack that inflicts high knockback and [[status:Blind]]. Gains [[status:All Stats Up]] when affected by el element effects, which includes the aforementioned attack.
* Its attack has the el element, so it will [[status:Blind]] units standing on [[obj:Dirt]] (such as [[ability:Mountain Form]] cats).
wikiTrivia: * They use a pitched male80 voice for cats, voiced by Tonetta.

name: Angelic Kitten
description: Attracts units. Dooms what kills it.   Immune to Holy. Gains All Stats Up when struck with Holy element.
wikiBehavior:
* Its melee attack deals 0 damage, but inflicts [[status:Poison]].
* At medium range, it inflicts [[status:Attraction]] on all units in an area.
* Inflicts [[status:Doomed]] on death and leaves a corpse.
wikiTrivia:
* This cat's appearance resembles Guppy, Edmund's deceased cat who is featured in many of his games.
* This enemy's somewhat-unkind behavior has some Biblical precedent, mainly with "the Satan" in the Book of Job.
* It is not clear why the Angelic Kitten enemies aren't swaddled up, while the "Peeker" and unlock art versions are.

name: Ankylosaurus
description: Has a wide melee attack with Knockback 10 and a chance to inflict Stun.  Does a spin attack when it takes damage.
wikiBehavior:
* It has a wide melee attack with 10 Knockback. This has a chance to [[status:Stun]].
* When damaged, it does a spin attack that hits all nearby tiles, including diagonal ones. This inflicts [[status:Bruise]].
** If downed but not instantly destroyed, it will still perform the spin attack.
* It starts each battle with [[status:Brace]] and [[status:Thorns]].
wikiTrivia: * wikipedia was an armored ornithiscian dinosaur belonging to the group Ankylosauria from the very end of the Cretaceous period.

name: Astronaut
description: Its melee attack has a high chance to inflict Stun.
wikiBehavior:
Astronauts are Cats, with a taser-like basic attack and a Movement ability.
* Astro Zapper: An Electric-element Magic attack with melee range. It has a 70% chance to [[status:Stun]].
* Space Jump: An unnamed movement ability, which has the Astronaut jump long distances.
wikiTrivia:
* There is no indication as to why Astronaut enemies need space helmets, when the player's cats do not.

* Astronaut might be a reference to the fact that in early days of space programs, various animals have been sent to space including cats.
** Astronaut itself could be a reference to wikipedia the first cat to make it to space.
* Their level editor icon is a reference to the game wikipedia, a game featuring coloured astronauts as playable characters.

name: Atomic Kitten
description: Emits a burst of radiation at the start of its turn. Teleports away when damaged. Explodes when killed.
wikiBehavior:
Atomic Kitten always starts protected with 2 [[status:Holy Shield]]. 
It starts it's turn by explosion attack in a range 2 that triggers, damaging and significantly knocking back all affected units, except ones that can be mutated. 
Moves by teleporting. 
Additionally, it teleports to a random tile when hit, and explodes, damaging all 8 tiles next to it, when killed. 
Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia:
* Atomic Kittens have a design heavily inspired by the DC Comics character Doctor Manhattan originally from the Watchmen series.
** Manhattan's design is also referenced in the item costume for tboi in The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth.
* Atomic Kitten  might be a reference to the English girl band of the same name.
dangerFlag: Explodes in range 2 at start of turn, teleports when hit, and explodes again on death.

name: B-Prober
description: Melee attacker. If it can melee attack a cat from behind it will inflict Charm. This Charm lasts until the Charmed cat takes damage.
wikiBehavior: B-Prober is a melee attacker. Backstabs from this unit inflict a special variety of [[status:Charmed]] that lasts until the next time the target takes damage.
wikiTrivia:
* B-Prober charming its enemy if it hits them from the back might be a reference to the first South Park episode [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartman_Gets_an_Anal_Probe|Cartman Gets an Anal Probe]] where Cartman, one of the four characters from the main cast is kidnapped by aliens and anally probed.
** Conversely, the trope of anal probes has many different competing sources. The most cited source is [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communion_(book)|the 1987 story "Communion" by Whitley Strieber,]] which describes such an event as done to him, popularizing it.
* The appearance of B-Probers are potentially a reference to the wikipedia trope.

name: Baby Deathworm
description: Dash attacks units that end their movement in line with it.  Can't dash backwards!
wikiBehavior:
Dashes at enemies that end their movement in line with it. Cannot dash backwards. This attack has [[status:Lifesteal]]. 
Moves by burrowing, avoiding all hazards outside of its end point.

name: Baby Shark
description: Its bite inflicts Bleed but does no damage. Takes bonus turns for each bleeding unit. Focuses on bleeding units.
wikiBehavior: The Baby Shark only has one attack, being a 0 damage melee attack that inflicts [[status:Bleed]]. However, it will prioritize attacking bleeding units and gains an extra turn per unique bleeding unit. Both of these behaviors do not discriminate between allies and enemies, meaning a bleeding allied unit is both a valid attack target and gives it an extra turn.
wikiTrivia:
* Both this enemy and the Daddy Shark are references to the children's song Baby Shark" that was popularized by the [[url:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XqZsoesa55w|"Baby Shark Dance"]] YouTube video by South Korean entertainment company Pinkfong.
* The blood-thirsty behaviors of this enemy are based on the pop cultural myth that sharks can smell blood from incredible distances, and can be sent into a frenzy by its presence.

name: Baby Squirrel
wikiBehavior: Unlike the adult squirrel it can attack only once per turn.

name: Bat
description: Its melee flurry inflicts Confusion. 50% Dodge Chance. Flying.
attackStyle: Melee attack, Multihit 4 Chance to inflict Confusion 1
wikiBehavior:
The Bat is a weak but agile enemy with permanent [[status:Flying]], a [[status:Dodge Chance]], and is notably one of very few enemies to have a non-standard [[stat:LCK]] stat, boasting 8 [[stat:LCK]] instead of the usual 5, further improving its ability to dodge attacks.

On its turn, the Bat will move towards a target and use a multi-hitting melee attack, dealing 1 damage 4 times. Each hit has a chance to inflict [[status:Confusion]]. 

If a Bat is targeted by an attack, regardless of if it got hit or dodged it, it will immediately retreat from the attacker.
wikiTrivia:
* According to Edmund, Bats are supposed to be annoying "Like Zubat in caves in Pokemon".
** Also like Zubat, they don't have legs or eyes, and inflict confusion.
dangerFlag: Multi-hit melee attack (1 damage x4 hits). High luck makes it dodge frequently.

name: Bear
wikiBehavior:
The Bear is a 2x2 melee unit with a basic attack that hits 2 tiles in front of it. 
It has [[status:Trample]] and its basic attack inflicts [[status:Bleed]].
wikiTrivia:
* The regular Bear is colored like the brown bear (Ursus arctos), second-largest of the eight bear species around today. The champion Bear is colored like the American black bear (Ursus americanus), who is smaller in real life.
** The two species have other differences as well; American black bears have more diversity in their fur colors, and a flatter back.

name: Beefy Leech
description: Melee Attacker.
wikiBehavior:
* The Beefy Leech has a melee attack with [[status:Lifesteal]]. This Lifesteal also Heal the Leech's owner by the same amount.
* Attacks enemies in melee range.
* Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia: * [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leech|Leeches]] are Annelids (like earthworms), belonging to the class Clitellata (also like earthworms) and the subclass Hirudinea.

name: Belcher
description: Its ranged attack inflict Burn and creates a lava tile. Immune to fire.
wikiBehavior:
* Immune to [[status:Burn]] and fire damage, such as bombs and [[obj:Lava]]
* Attacks by spitting a lava shot within range 2 from itself. Will attack ground if no better targets available.

name: Best Bud (Familiar)
description: Melee attacker.
wikiBehavior: Best Bud has a melee attack that heals it's summoner.

name: Big Asteroid
description: Its attack spawns a boulder. Gets knocked back with Chain Knockback when hit. Can only recieve 1 damage at a time. Immune to status effects.
wikiBehavior:
Floats. Immune to status effects. 
Attacks by lobbing a single [[obj:Boulder]] within 3-tile straight line, perfectly accurate unlike its lesser counterpart. 
Has chain knockback when it gets hit. Can only take one damage at a time (2 on critical hits).

name: Birthwort
description: Blind. Can melee attack and dash with Trample in random directions. Fires shots that inflict Rot whenever it's attacked. Heals itself and its neighbors at the end of its turn.
wikiBehavior:
Blind. Will melee attack if it starts turn adjacent to enemy. Spawns grass where it moves. 
Dashes in random direction after moving, [[status:Trample]] everything on way. 
When damaged, shoots a straight-line shot from both its sides (not front and back). These shots inflict [[status:Rot]] on whoever they hit. 
Heals itself and any adjacent allies for 2 HP at the end of its every turn. 
Immune to [[status:Poison]].

name: Bishop Hat
description: Attracts Cultists.   Can be picked up by a Cultist to promote them into a Bishop.
wikiBehavior:
* No actions on its own.
* Attracts Cultist lackies and Cultist Zealots.
* Can be picked up by an adjacent Cultist to promote them into a Cultist Bishop.
* Cultist Bishops drop their Bishop Hat on death, allowing another Cultist to promote.
** The dropped Bishop Hat will be at full health.
* If given a turn (by Love Bot for example), it will move away from the player's cats.
wikiTrivia: * Bishop Hat resembles a piece of [[obj:Mini Nuke]], which spawn in The Bunker.

name: Black Bird
description: Whoever kills this gets +1 All Stats Up and finds a bonus item at the end  of the combat!
wikiBehavior:
Like all bonus birds, Black Birds are passive, neutral units that will move to a random tile each turn. 
When attacked (and alive after), they will retaliate against the target with a peck (if the target is adjacent to them) and flee to a random tile.

Black Birds will flee from the battle on their first turn.

Black Birds will grant whatever kills them with [[status:All Stats Up]] for the remainder of the battle. This includes enemy and in-animate units. 
If a friendly unit kills them, the player will be rewarded with a random item after the battle.

If the we weather is in play, it will become a hostile neutral entity, meaning it actively attack the enemy and player units in equal measure. In addition to no longer fleeing the battle after a set amount of turns.

name: Blorb
description: "Its ranged attack inflicts Slow in an area."
wikiBehavior: Blorb is a ranged attacker that tries to keep its distance while firing a projectile that deals 3 damage and inflicts [[status:Slow]] to units in an area.

name: Bombchu (Familiar)
wikiBehavior:
Bombchu will keep distance from enemies until it has an enemy in a straight line across from it.

It will then dash at the enemy, exploding on hit and dealing 5 el and el damage and 1 knockback in a 1 radius circle around it.
* In essence, its attack is same as the [[ability:Rocket Skates]] ability.
* Will explode on death, with same damage and radius.
wikiTrivia: * [[url:https://zeldawiki.wiki/wiki/Bombchu|Bombchus]] are recurring explosive items in The Legend of Zelda series.

name: Bone Worm
description: Ranged Attacker. Gains more range the taller it becomes. Loses height when it takes damage. Can only take one damage at a time when tall. Undead.
wikiBehavior:
* The Bone Worm is a stationary ranged attacker who every turn, in addition to attacking, adds some bones to itself and grows taller by 1 (up to height of 3). Every unit of height increases its range by 1 and gives it [[status:Damage Up]].
* Attacking it when its height is more than 1 will reduce all damage dealt to it to 1, but decrease its height by 1.

name: Boomer
description: Explodes when killed, damaging all nearby units.
wikiBehavior:
* Uses a melee attack with 4 damage and Knockback 1. 
* Upon death, explodes, dealing 5 el damage with Knockback 1 to all units on adjacent or diagonally adjacent tiles. 
** Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia:
* Potentially inspired by [[url:https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/The_Boomer|The Boomer]] from [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2|Left 4 Dead 2.]]
* Its appearance, with swollen lips and eyelids, a bloated abdomen, and bluish skin, makes the Boomer resemble a drowned body.
dangerFlag: Explodes on death dealing 5 damage to all adjacent and diagonal tiles.

name: Bounty Hunter (Enemy)
description: Can shoot anywhere within its line of sight. Prefers long shots.
wikiBehavior: A ranged attacker with unlimited range, but with a line-of-sight requirement.
wikiTrivia:
* Bounty Hunters have an alternative appearance when spawned from the Weather weather effect.
** Bounty Hunters spawned this way prioritize shooting the Bounty and run away with it once the Bounty is downed.
* Both its hat and its poncho are pieces of equipment, thus they can be destroyed by a Skull Ooze's ranged attack or stolen by a Maelestes.

name: Bounty Hunter (Event Enemy)
description: Can shoot anywhere within its line of sight. Prefers long shots.
wikiBehavior: During the Bounty Hunting a Bounty Hunter will spawn in every battle and attempt to kill a random unit (either an enemy or one of the player's cats) in the level before exiting it.
wikiTrivia: * Despite sharing the same name as the Bounty Hunter enemy from the [[chapter:Desert]], this enemy has a different appearance that's exclusive to the weather weather.

name: Brain Drain
description: Infinite ranged magic attacker. Will counter a spell once per turn. If it starts its turn with its counterspell still available, it absorbs it for a buff.
wikiBehavior:
* Will try to keep maximum distance from its enemies and attack with its infinite range basic attack, that deals magical damage.
* At the end of each of its turns, it primes its counterspell, meaning the next spell cast by one of its enemies will do nothing. The caster will still lose the appropriate amount of mana when this happens.
** If it starts its turn with its counterspell still primed, it will lose the counterspell and give itself [[status:All Stats Up]] and [[status:Damage Up]]. It also will heal 8 health.
wikiTrivia: *  Brain drain is a phenomenon consisting in the emigration of highly educated, talented or intelligent individuals from their home country to another, typically seeking better job opportunities.

name: Bramble Baby
description: Spawns Bramble tiles and pulls units into them.
wikiBehavior:
Moves by burrowing down and reappearing on other empty tile. Spawns [[obj:Bramble]] on adjacent tiles, usually after moving. If it spawns brambles below a unit they become entangled. 
Can pull units in, by shooting a harpoon-like vine.
wikiTrivia: * Although the champion version has 2 stalks, the animations mostly use the 1 stalk version, even though the double does exist in the files and used for the Amoeba.

name: Brute
description: Throws rocks that have a chance inflict Stun when at range. Will uppercut units above 50% health. Will instantly kill units below 50% health. Immune to fire.
wikiBehavior:
* Immune to [[status:Burn]] and fire damage like bombs and lava tiles.
Will attempt to move towards enemies to melee attack them.
* Can throw a [[obj:Small Rock]] at any unit, that deal 5 damage and have a 20% chance of inflicting [[status:Stun]].
* Uppercuts their enemies who are at more than 50% HP, dealing 5 damage and knocking them back 3 tiles.
* Instantly downs units who are at less than 50% HP in melee range.
dangerFlag: Instantly downs any unit below 50% HP with an uppercut.

name: Bunga's Champion
description: One of Lord Bunga's top guys!
wikiBehavior:
* The Champions will attempt to throw their spear at the player's cats. If hit, it will inflict [[status:Stun]]. They will prioritize retrieving their spear and will [[status:Trample]] units on the way.
* Without their spear, they gain access to a powerful 3 hit combo that can quickly kill downed cats.
* They have access to spells used by the other caveman (Caveman Man, Caveman Woman, Caveman Baby and Wereman).
* When unable to attack, they may use a war cry called "Frooga Bunga!", giving themselves and allies within 3 tiles [[status:Damage Up]]. This may also give them [[status:Madness]].
* They might prioritize attacking the lowest health cat when possible (needs further testing).cn

name: Burfer Maggot
description: Its attack surrounds units with Thorny lumps.
attackStyle: Lobbed attack, Range 2 Surrounds the attacked unit with Thorny Lumps
wikiBehavior: * Burfer Maggots are much reviled for their Tumor Prison spell, which surrounds a unit on all four cardinal directions with Tumors. These Tumors have only 1 HP, but they also have [[status:Thorns]].

name: Butch & Tink
description: Moves 1 tile toward whatever damages them.  Will dash on their last turn.  Trample.
wikiBehavior:
Butch & Tink is almost functionally identical to Boris, serving as a simple reskin with an adjusted amount of [[stat:HEALTH]] (160) and [[stat:SPD]]. 

It should be noted that this enemy has two "fronts" and no back, meaning that landing backstabs is impossible. Butch & Tink never turn 180 degrees while moving, and will approach you with whichever face is most convenient for them.
wikiTrivia: * This enemy is allusion to the possibility that Butch and Tink may have been [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjoined_twins|conjoined twins]] in the past.

name: Butt Zombie
description: Will attack all adjacent units with its melee attack when its backside is underground. Goes upside down when damaged. Undead.
attackStyle: Melee attack, Consecutively hits every adjacent unit
wikiBehavior:
Moves by digging down and reappearing on empty tile of its choice, bypassing any obstacles and hazards. After digging itself up, melees every adjacent unit, one by one. 
Flips over when damaged. After being damaged while upside down, it will fart, knocking back all adjacent units and inflicting [[status:Poison]] 4. Also farts if it begins its turn upside down. Its movement action flips it back to upright position. 
Does not leave a corpse.

name: Cancer Cat
description: Its melee attack causes cats it hits to lose 1 Constitution permanently and has a chance to give them cancer.
wikiBehavior:
* Cancer Cat will attack with a melee attack that inflicts [[status:Constitution Down]], and has a 30% chance to inflict [[disorder:Cancer]].
* After three turns elapse, it will explode, leaving [[obj:Gas Cloud]] and a Carcass behind.

Starts with 2 brace.
dangerFlag: Melee attack has 30% chance to inflict Cancer disorder. Explodes after 3 turns.

name: Carcass
description: Spawns random types of Maggots.
wikiBehavior: * Spawns either a Maggot, Chargey Maggot, Diggy Maggot, or Burfer Maggot.

name: Carnibulb
description: Will instantly kill anything it can reach.
wikiBehavior:
* Spawns one Sprout on random tile at end of its turn.
* Gains one [[stat:MOV]] per Sprout, giving it ability to move.
* Has insta-kill melee attack.
** This only deals 25 damage against bosses.
* Immune to [[status:Poison]], [[obj:Creep]], heals from el.
* Has [[status:Trample]].
wikiTrivia: * Carnibulb may be based on Audrey II, from the comedy horror musical [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Shop_of_Horrors_(1986_film)|Little Shop of Horrors]].
dangerFlag: Has an insta-kill melee attack. Also has Trample.

name: Cat Caller
description: Slows units. Counterattacks when hit.
wikiBehavior:
* Inflicts [[status:Slow]] on an enemy up to 6 tiles away.
* Counter attacks melee attackers. 
* If there are no damage-dealing allies left, it will run.
wikiTrivia:
* Its design seems to be similar to the concept of a human cat caller, that is, someone who makes inappropriate comments about others, often sexual in nature.
* Cat Caller look and behave similar to Siren.
* They use a female4 voice for cats, voiced by Lisa Kuras.

name: Cat Cultist
description: Melee attacker. Increases the amount of times it can attack each turn whenever it takes damage.
wikiBehavior: Melee attacker that gains additional attacks per turn each time it is damaged. Damages itself on its turn.

name: Catbot (Familiar)
wikiBehavior:
Catbot will attempt to use the weapon given to it, consuming weapon's durability as usual.
* If given electric weapon (such as [[item:Stun Gun]]) it may try to [[status:Energized]] other robot allies instead of attacking.
* If made without a weapon, lost its weapon due to it running out of uses or given a non-offensive weapon slot item (such as [[item:Mini Jetpack]]) catbot will be unable to attack, but will still try to move next to the enemies to bodyblock them.

name: Caterpillar
description: Gains All Stats Up each turn. Evolves into a Moth when it reaches All Stats Up 5.
wikiBehavior: A melee attacker that has a pitiful 1 damage, movement range, and luck. At the end of each turn, it gains [[status:All Stats Up]]. Upon reaching [[status:All Stats Up]], it turns into a Moth.

name: Caveman Baby
description: Has a melee attack with Lifesteal. Seeks food. Will grow up when it reaches full health.
wikiBehavior:
Caveman Babies start battles at half health. They are standard melee units that attempt to get close to a target and attack it, dealing Physical Damage. This attack has a [[status:Lifesteal]] effect, healing the Baby equivalent to the damage it deals.

Caveman Babies can also seek out and consume [[obj:Food]] pickups to heal themslves.

Once the Baby heals itself to full, it will "grow up" into a Caveman Man.
wikiTrivia: * A Caveman Baby is seen riding on Lord Bunga's back during the first phase of the fight.

name: Caveman Chief
description: Its melee attack inflicts Stun. Goes for killing blows against enemies with 10 or fewer HP. Buffs its humanoid allies. Hates Cats!
wikiBehavior: Gives all stats up to humanoid allies. Its melee attack inflicts stun, hits all units in its range, and has +1 reach. Insta-kills, with no corpse, enemies with 10 or fewer HP. ”Hates Cats!” (It treats Sabertooth and Mammoth units as enemies.) Starts with 15 shield. Can use its action to give an ally an extra turn. Its buff to humanoids also applies to player aligned humanoids. Will insta-kill objects such as rocks.
dangerFlag: Insta-kills enemies with 10 or fewer HP. Gives All Stats Up to all humanoid allies.

name: Caveman Man
description: Has a multi-hit melee attack. Will attempt to pick up spears. Hates Cats!
wikiBehavior:
The Caveman Man's behavior differs on whether or not he has a spear in his possession.

* If he has a spear, he will move towards a target in range and throw it at them, [[status:Stun]] them and leaving the spear lodged in the ground.
** The spear becomes an Object with 12 HP that can be attacked and destroyed. Attacking it will knock it it up and away, damaging and bouncing off of whatever it hits.
* If he does not have a spear, he will prioritize getting another one. If there is one within range, he will run towards it with [[status:Trample]] and pick it back up. If there aren't any reachable spears, he will instead run to a nearby target and use a multi-hitting melee attack that knocks up and inflicts [[status:Bruise]].
* In either stance, if there aren't any valid targets he will instead move to nearby allies and give both them and himself a damage up. May only affect fellow Cavemen units, testing required.cn

Additionally, the Caveman Man considers all Mammoth and Sabertooth units enemies.
* If he is attacked by a Sabertooth Cat or Sabertooth Kitten, he has a chance to become a Wereman.

name: Caveman Woman
description: Will use cats as weapons.  Pregnant!
wikiBehavior:
Occasionally spawns a Caveman Baby on adjacent tiles.

Can pick up cats, using them to attack an area in front of her.

name: Chain Demon
description: Will hook and pull units toward itself. Immune to fire.
wikiBehavior:
Is fire immune. 
Has a hook and can pull units towards itself, though only in cardinal straight lines. Has a el melee attack that deals damage and inflicts [[status:Burn]].

name: Chaos Stacy
description: Its melee attack inflicts Scrambled.
wikiBehavior:
Chaos Stacies will perform a two-pronged melee attack to any target they can reach. They will:
# Rotate the target so that it is facing away from the Chaos Stacy. This inflicts [[status:Scrambled]] on the target.
# Knock the target away - dealing damage to the cat and anything they collide with.

Stacy will also passively [[status:Reflect]] any incoming projectiles, and automatically knock back melee attackers by 2 tiles.
wikiTrivia:
* Despite Chaos Stacy's "Damage" being listed as 0, they do deal melee damage with the second part of their melee attack.
* Like other enemies in the rift, Chaos Stacy is related to the NPC Stacy #515731 who resides with Dr. Beanie at the start of the game.
* Chaos Stacy has 26 Base Health and 5 Base Luck, but it's actual stats differ due to mutations:
**  a mutation
**  a mutation: [[stat:LCK]]
**  a mutation: [[stat:LCK]], [[stat:CON]]
**  a mutation: [[stat:LCK]]

name: Chargey Maggot
description: Its dash attack has trample.
wikiBehavior: It charges at you.

name: Cherub
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up and finds a bonus item!
wikiTrivia:
* [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherub|Cherubs]] are the most frequently-cited angels in the Hebrew Bible. They are divine beings of some higher rank than messenger angels. Their exact Hebrew portrayal is somewhat unclear, but understood to be a somewhat-animalistic form with a human head. The Christian New Testament associates them with the four-faced "[[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living_creatures_(Bible)|living creatures]]" in Ezekiel 1, while Medieval art typically portrays them as plump boys with wings.
* In the fourth phase of the fight, The Creator's "Father" form knocks out several Cherub corpses when attacking. They can be revived via [[item:Smelling Salts]], [[ability:Awaken]], or any other revival spell that works on non-allied units in order to kill them again for an [[status:All Stats Up]].

name: Cherubim
description: Gives its allies Holy Shield. Primes an area attack when damaged. Immune to Holy. Gains All Stats Up when struck with Holy Element.
wikiBehavior: Cherubim are a [[status:Flying]] enemy that begin combat with several stacks of [[status:Holy Shield]]. Initially, they will not attempt to directly attack the player's party; their only attack is Bless. When they are attacked by an enemy unit, Cherubim will fly out of the battlefield, become untargetable, and prime Careen on the cat who performed the attack. If the assailant was a non-cat unit like a Familiar, the attack will be primed on one of the player's cats at random.
wikiTips:
* Because Cherubim will never attempt to deal direct damage unless retaliated against, it is safe to heal and stack buffs against them once Cherubim are the only remaining enemies. Be careful of being outscaled by their [[status:All Stats Up]] and [[status:Holy Shield]] stacking, however.
* Multi-hit attacks such as [[ability:Fury Swipes]] will only deal damage once, after which the Cherubim will prime an attack and become untargetable.
* If a single cat damages multiple Cherubims, all of them will prime an attack in the same spot, causing them to dash into each other and inflict damage and [[status:Stun]] on themselves.
* Shield-piercing effects like [[status:Marked]] greatly simplify dealing with this enemy.
* The [[status:Immobile]] and [[status:Stun]] statuses prevents the Cherubim from flying away from battlefield.
** Because they are [[status:Flying]] enemies, el-element attacks will [[status:Immobile]] them, making them highly effective.
* Any mutations or items that trigger [[status:Kinetic Spikes]] upon taking damage are not recommended against Cherubims. If a sparkle hits a Cherubim, the cat that produced it will be targeted and hit, assuming the player lacks the means to escape the attack. If the cat is hit by Careen, it will produce another sparkle which instantly hits the Cherubim, causing it to immediately prime it's attack again. As the cat will almost certainly be stunned from the attack, this will effectively stunlock the cat to death. This is especially dangerous with the champion version.
** By extension, the [[class:Mage]]'s passive ability [[ability:Light Up the Stage]] is also strongly advised against, as the sparkles are emitted at the end of the Mage's turn, effectively making the Mage a sitting duck for Cherubims to target.
** If the player has the means of controlling sparkles (E.G. [[item:Sacred Heart]], [[class:Monk]]'s active ability [[ability:Release Energy]], etc), they can be very helpful, as the player can trigger Cherubims to land in a single spot and safely escape. This is great for chipping away at their holy shields, and as an added bonus, they'll slam into and [[status:Stun]] each other too.
* Knock back damage does not make them retaliate.
wikiTrivia:
* This enemy is based on the wikipedia from the Abrahamic traditions. The additional eyes and uncreaturelike shape are based on the wikipedia, and/or the wikipedia.
* One of the Peekers in the Infinite is an upside-down Cherubim, whose plumage resembles a kitty face (:3). 
** This detail can also be observed in combat.

name: Chicken
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up and finds a bonus item!
wikiBehavior:
Like most bonus birds, Chickens are passive, neutral units that will move to a random tile each turn.
When attacked (and alive after), they will retaliate against the target with a peck (if the target is adjacent to them) and flee to a random tile.

Chickens will flee from the battle on their third turn.

Chickens will grant whatever kills them with [[status:All Stats Up]] for the remainder of the battle. This includes enemy units.
If a friendly unit kills them, the player will be rewarded with a random item after the battle.

If the "Birdemic" weather is in play, it will become a hostile neutral entity, meaning it actively attack the enemy and player units in equal measure. In addition to no longer fleeing the battle after a set amount of turns.
wikiTrivia:
* [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken|Chickens]] are domesticated junglefowl of the order [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galliformes|Galliformes]], which Turkeys are also a part of.
** Galliformes is roughly Latin for "rooster-like".

name: Chum Bag
description: Its long range attack spawns Maggots if it hits an empty tile. Becomes a Chummy when killed. Stationary.
attackStyle: Lobbed attack, Range 5 Blind spot, Range 2
wikiBehavior:
* If it can hit an enemy:
** Lobs a projectile at it.
* If no enemies are in range:
** Targets an empty tile, spawning a Maggot. 
* Turns into a Chummy when it dies.
wikiTrivia:
* Spawns pickups when hit with [[item:Crowbar]].
* This enemy bears a resemblance to the Pokémon Trubbish.

name: Chummy
description: Dashes in a straight line.
wikiBehavior:
* Spawns from Chum Bag. 
* Attempts to align itself cardinally with its enemies in order to perform a long range dash attack which has Knockback.
* Will target units behind cover if said cover is able to be knocked into the unit.

name: Cloaked Demon
description: Casts an area spell that inflicts Burn 3 to enemies and gives +1 Damage to allies. Inflicts Hex on units that damage it. Immune to fire.
wikiBehavior:
Immune to [[status:Burn]] and fire damage, such as bombs and lava tiles. 
Its only combat move is casting a charged, allegiance-sensitive spell "Twisting flames", that targets a radius 2 area. 
Allies in radius will be healed for 3 HP and granted [[status:Damage Up]]. 
Enemies in radius will receive 3 [[status:Burn]]. 
Inflicts [[status:Hex]] on units that damage it. 
Harmed by Holy heals.
wikiTrivia:
* Cloaked Demons are one of very few units that can apply Hex.
** The only others are Tatters and Guillotina 3.

name: Clot
description: Has a chance to become a Stem Cat at the end of the turn.
wikiBehavior:
Attempts to flee from your cats. 

Clots do not have attacks. Instead they do one of the following each turn, with a 50-50 chance:
* "Evolve" into a Stem Cat
* "Fail to Evolve" (resulting in nothing happening)

name: Conjoined Husk
description: Its melee attack picks up cats.
wikiBehavior:
Its melee attack picks up cats.
Creates evil copies of cats it's holding.

name: Cop Bot
description: Melee attacker. Will shoot at enemies who damage its allies.
wikiBehavior:
All attacks that contact the front of the Cop Bot will be blocked by its riot shield.

Like other robot units, Cop Bot get's [[status:Energized]] when affected by El elements.

Cop Bot will retaliate against any enemies that attack its allies. It does this by firing a single projectile in a straight line at the target.

It starts with 1 ammo, and will load an additional unit of ammo every round.

Cop Bots will target downed cats to melee and trample them.

If there are no non-Cop-Bot units left alive on the enemy's side, it will deactivate.

They also have [[status:Trample]], displacing any enemies they collide with.
wikiTrivia:
* Cop Bots can be heard saying the words “Reloading!” when reloading their weapons and “HE’S GOT A GUN!” when firing, "HE'S GOT A GUN!" is a joke based on corrupt cops and police brutality.
* Cop Bots using a melee attack on downed cats is likely a joke based on police brutality.

name: Core Freak
description: Can perform a flurry melee attack or a headbutt that inflicts stun. Blind.
wikiBehavior:
The Core Freak has two main attacks it can use:
; Headbuttcn
: The Core Freak slams its head onto an adjacent tile, dealing 5 Physical Damage and inflicting [[status:Stun]].
; Fury
: The Core Freak attacks thrice onto an adjacent tile, dealing 3x3 Physical Damage.
wikiTrivia: * Core Freaks resemble the mutants from the [[chapter:Bunker]].

name: Crater Creeper
description: Shoots rocks or dashes forward leaving an Amoeba behind.
wikiBehavior:
* Will dash with [[status:Trample]] and leave [[obj:Creep]] on tiles it dashes through. Leaves an Amoeba behind when it does.
* Will sometimes shoot a [[obj:Small Rock]] at its targets if close.
* Is considered a [[type:Rock]] in its first stage, and as such can be picked up by amoebas.
* Has a second "out" stage which needs to be killed again. In this stage it can teleport to [[obj:Creep]] and is no longer considered a rock type.
wikiTrivia: * It is the enemy version of mb.

name: Cultist Bishop
description: Its lightning attack has a chance to Stun. Heals its allies. Spawns a Bishop Hat when killed.
wikiBehavior:
* The Bishop innately has [[status:Flying]], [[status:Kinetic Spikes]], and [[status:Holy Shield]].
* Attacks in an ordinal X shape that deals 5 Electric damage and has 25% chance to inflict [[status:Stun]].
:
* Occasionally blesses all their allied units, healing them for 5 HP and giving them [[status:Damage Up]] for rest of the battle.
* Spawns a Bishop Hat on death, instead of a corpse.
wikiTrivia:
* The Bishop's diagonal attack pattern is a reference to the movement behavior of the bishop piece from chess, which can only move across the board in diagonal lines.
** Likewise, the behavior of other cultists "promoting" themselves to a Bishop is like a reference to the promotion mechanic in chess, in which a pawn can be replaced with another, better piece (including a bishop) when it reaches the opposite end of the board.
*** Ironically, promotion to a Bishop is the rarest form of promotion in chess.
* The internal nickname for all cultists is 'BunkerBoy', found within the game's files.

name: Cultist Lackey
description: Melee attacker that throws units. Becomes a Zealot when it kills something.
wikiBehavior:
Cultist Lackeys are melee attackers that can either swat at enemies with a 5 damage melee attack, or throw units around the map, including at its enemies. 

Lackeys are notable for the several transformations they can undergo depending on the circumstances, including:
* When they kill something, they become a Cultist Zealot. 
* If they can reach a Bishop Hat, they will put it on and get promoted to a Cultist Bishop. 
* Can becomes a Cultist Mutant if it moves over a [[obj:Toxic Waste]] or takes damage from a [[obj:Mini Nuke]] or Atomic Kitten.

Cultist Lackeys are also spawned as part of the Johnny boss fight, wherein they will attempt to move towards the center of the arena where the boss is located in order to begin washing him. They will not move or attack while they are doing so, but may toss other units away in order to reach Johnny. When Johnny is killed, all Cultist Lackeys currently alive will immediately turn into Cultist Zealots.
wikiTrivia:
* Johnny and his followers are heavily implied by npc to be npc' unsuccessful human experiments that he dumped into the [[chapter:The Bunker]].
* Cultists may follow Johnny because of his mind control abilities.
** Alternatively, lackeys turning into zealots upon Johnny's death may mean that they followed him genuinely.
* The cultists are sometimes refered to as 'BunkerBoy' in the game's files.
* Cultists can be seen in the core’s cutscene when you unlock the area.

name: Cultist Mutant
description: Does a wide melee attack that knocks units into the air. Spawns a Tumor when it dies. Brace 2.
wikiBehavior:
The Cultist Mutant is a slow melee attacker that innately gets two turns per round and has [[status:Brace]]. If it gets in range it has a three-tile wide melee attack that lobs units back, dealing 4 damage plus any additional damage incurred on landing.

Cultist Lackeys and Cultist Zealots can transform into Cultist Mutants either upon touching a [[obj:Toxic Waste]] or being affected by other sources of "radioactive" damage, such as the energy burst from an Atomic Kitten or a [[obj:Mini Nuke]] explosion. This does not change their [[stat:HEALTH]].

The Cultist Mutant does not leave a corpse on death, instead spawning a Blorb or a Florb.
wikiTrivia: * The cultists are sometimes referred to as 'BunkerBoy' in the game's files.
dangerFlag: Two turns per round with a three-tile-wide melee attack that lobs units.

name: Cultist Zealot
description: Does a multi-stab attack.  Gains +1 damage at the end of its turn.  Becomes suicidal when at low HP.
wikiBehavior:
The Cultist Zealot is a melee attacker that can choose between two melee attacks, and will use Cut on itself at the end of its turn. When their health is lowered to 30% or less, they will pull out a large bomb and enter a "suicidal" state. Killing them while they have a bomb out will cause them to explode, damaging adjacent units.
Cultist Zealots will become a Cultist Mutant if it takes el damage, which is most frequently inflicted by walking over [[obj:Toxic Waste]] or taking damage from a [[obj:Mini Nuke]] or Atomic Kitten.
wikiTrivia:
* The internal nickname for all cultists is 'BunkerBoy', found within the game's files.
* The symbol on the Regular Cultist Zealot resembles an atom symbol. This is more apparent in its turn order icon.
** Similar symbols appear in Johnny's background intro art, implying that the symbol carries some sort of significance among the Cultists.
** The champion version appears to have a symbol vaguely resembling the Difficulty icons instead.

name: Daddy Shark
description: Will instantly kill anything it can reach! Gains bonus turns for each bleeding unit. Focuses on bleeding units.
wikiBehavior:
Prioritizes any unit with the [[status:Bleed]] status, including allies over other enemies.
Instantly kills 1 adjacent target eating it and restoring health.
Typically spawns trapped in a certain area.
wikiTrivia:
* Daddy Shark's name might have come from the children's song [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Shark|"Baby Shark"]], in which a "Daddy Shark" is mentioned. Additionally, the enemy's reveal on [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter|Twitter/X]] was accompanied by the verse of the song where the "Daddy Shark" is mentioned.
* Daddy Shark's attack power is listed as "infinity", which is presumably how it gets around the typical instakill resistance on Bosses.
dangerFlag: Insta-kills one adjacent target by eating it. Prioritizes units with Bleed.

name: Death Worm
description: Digs underground after its dash attack. Will eat any unit that ends movement on top of it while it's underground.
wikiBehavior: Uses a charge attack. 2x2 size, and kills (definitely) anything that stands on it when it is burrowed.
wikiTrivia: • Could be a reference to the Mongolian death worm cryptid, the sandworms from the Dune series of novels, or the "grabboids" from the 1990 film Tremors.

name: Death!
description: He's here to take what he's owed.
wikiBehavior:
Death is very similar to Reaper in terms of attacks and appearance - though he has much more health.

Unlike every other event exclusive encounter, Death! is not a boss.

name: Deathbot (Familiar)
wikiBehavior: Will use a flamethrower ability to attack in a 3 tile line in front of it, dealing 3 damage and applying [[status:Burn]] to the first unit hit as well as burn the tiles in between.

name: Demon Kitten
description: Its melee attack can hit multiple times!

name: Der Fötus
description: Multi-hit melee attacker.  Calls an airstrike when at low health.
wikiBehavior:
Der Fötus is a melee unit with a multi-hitting melee attack, dealing 2 damage per hit with a random number of hits.

When brought to low health, it will bring out a remote. Killing it while it has a remote out will prime an airstrike attack, which will damage everything in the marked area at the end of the round.
wikiTrivia:
* The name of this enemy is a loose pun on "[[url:https://supermeatboy.fandom.com/wiki/Dr._Fetus|Dr. Fetus]]", the name of the main antagonist from [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Meat_Boy|Super Meat Boy]], who these enemies resemble heavily.
** This is even more noticeable when it's in its airstrike phase, since the remote it uses is the exact same Dr. Fetus uses in Super Meat Boy.
* The walking animation it has when there is a remote in its hand does not properly play the "footstep" sound effects.
dangerFlag: When killed at low health, primes an airstrike that damages everything in the marked area.

name: Diggy Maggot
description: Its melee attack has a chance to stun. Swaps places with a unit to move.
attackStyle: Melee attack Chance to inflict Stun 1
wikiBehavior:
* Despite the 20 points of Movement, Diggy Maggots can only move through their Switch ability, which has them tunnel to another unit's spot (and tunnels that unit to the user's original spot).
* Their Melee attack is a lick, which does 7 damage and has a 25% chance to [[status:Stun]].
** The damage scales with their [[stat:STR]].
wikiTrivia: * Their lick attack having a chance to inflict stun is most likely a reference to the Pokémon move of the same name, which is a Ghost-type physical attack with a chance of inflicting paralysis.

name: Dino Nest
description: Spawns baby Raptors.
wikiBehavior: * Spawns a Raptor Kitten on its turn.

name: Dip
description: Melee attacker.
wikiBehavior:
Basic melee attacker, weak on its own. 
Spawned from stronger poop enemies, such as Piles and mb. 
Is a poop. Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia:
* Dip comes from the vulgar slang dipshit.
** They also previously appeared as an enemy in The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth.

name: Doktorbot
description: Heals its allies and gives them random buffs.  Spawns Invaders.  Collects pickups.
wikiBehavior: Der Doktorbot is a supportive enemy that primarily foucses on healing its allies. It does this with a 3-hit move that heals and either gives a random buff or cleanses a random debuff per hit. If no allies are in range, it will instead seek out and collect pickups. If there are no pickups or allies nearby, it will instead spawn a Schpidenbot.

name: Dove
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up andfinds a bonus item!
wikiBehavior:
Neutral, does not attack anything on its own. When damaged attempts to hit back whoever hit it (if able) and flies away to some other tile.
Unit that kills it, gets bonus to all stats for the rest of the battle. Your party also gets a bonus item at end of the battle.
Runs from battle at the end of Round 1.
wikiTrivia:
* Doves are birds of the family [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbidae|Columbidae]], the same as that of Pigeons.
* Doves are recognized as a universal symbol of peace, which is referenced by it dropping items from the hippie set.

name: Dr. Beanies (Enemy)
description: Tosses bombs that explode at the end of the round.
wikiBehavior: Dr. Beanies is a reskin of Radical Rat, with identical behaviour and stats, though he is classified as a normal enemy rather than a boss, and a humanoid rather than a rat.
wikiTrivia:
* In his throwing animation, the bomb he produces resembles a cat instead of a rat for a small moment. The bomb spawned still resembles a rat, however.
* In champion version of his "turtle up" animation, "FANK IS HER" (npc is here) is written on his bucket, foreshadowing his fate at the end of the game.

name: Dr. Cat
description: Will randomly cast one of 6 spells.
wikiBehavior:
Casts 1 of 6 spells at random: 
* [[ability:Ping]]
* [[ability:Reduce]]
* [[ability:Shockwave]]
* [[ability:Stasis]]
* [[ability:Telefrag]]
* [[ability:Zealot]]

name: Dr. Ditto
description: Fires rockets that hit a random tile in an area.
wikiBehavior:
* Dr. Ditto will attempt to get near a cat, and attack with a ranged missile on a wide area, causing el on a random tile which will set plants on fire and deal knockback on its adjacent tiles.
* If Dr. Ditto starts its turn adjacent to an enemy, it will apply [[status:Fear]] to it before moving or attacking.
* When downed, Dr. Ditto will lay down on the floor and get back up if its body remains at the end of the round.
wikiTrivia:
* Dr Ditto may be a reference to the [[url:https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ditto_(Pok%C3%A9mon)|Pokemon of the same name]], as they both have crudely drawn faces and the ability to mimic.
* Its death animation appears to be a reference to the [[url:https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/family-guy-death-pose-peter-falls-down-the-stairs|Family Guy Death Pose]].

name: Draven's Crow
description: Melee attacker than can also use a wind attack with Knockback.  Will move and attack enemies that attack Draven.
wikiTrivia: * Although when summoned by Robo-Draven in the Hitler III fight they will be named as "Robo-Draven's Crow", their description still refers to regular Draven.

name: Druid's Crow
description: Inherits its owner's stats. Basic attack modifiers on its owner also get applied to the Crow. Flying.
wikiBehavior:
Druid's Crow is controlled by the player. It has three abilities:
* Its basic attack is [[ability:Melee Attack (Collarless)]].
* [[ability:Flutter]] allows it to fly exactly three tiles away for 5 mana. This ability ignores obstacles.
* [[ability:Aeroblast]] creates a gust of wind covering three tiles in a cardinal direction. Units in the gust take 1 damage and 1 knockback. This ability costs 5 mana and has the el element.

The Crow has all of its summoner's stats, including any stat ups the summoner had at the time of spawning.

Any basic attack modifiers the summoner has are shared with the Crow. The Crow can collect pickups like a party member.
wikiTrivia: * If you get a Crow through an event (such as the Cloning Tube in [[chapter:The Lab]]), it will be known as "Nobody's Crow" and it will have the stats of the cat who got the event.

name: Eagle
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up and finds a bonus item!
wikiBehavior: Eagles apply [[status:Bleed]] to units that they attack.
wikiTrivia:
* The Eagle resembles the [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bald_eagle|bald eagle]], both the national bird and national symbol of the United States of America.
** Its item pool is likely a reference to the prominent gun culture in the USA.

name: Edema
description: Evolves into a Husk when its timer reaches 0.
wikiBehavior:
The Edema does nothing other than count down a [[status:Transformation]] timer each turn. Upon reaching zero, it will evolve into a Husk.

On death it will spawn [[obj:Tumor]] that block movement and have [[status:Thorns]], similar to Burfer Maggot.
wikiTrivia:
* Edema is based on an enemy from [[url:https://theendisnigh.fandom.com/wiki/Enemies#Edema|The End is Nigh]].
* An edema is an instance of fluid build up under the body's tissue, causing swelling.

name: Egg (Familiar)
description: What could it hatch into?
wikiBehavior:
Can't move or attack.

After 2 turn will turn into one of the following, with equal chance:
# Squirrel
# Crow
# Snake
# Turtle
# Toad 
# Caterpillar
wikiTrivia:
* Shares its description with the Strange Egg.
* Its idle animation is only 1 frame (still image).
* The egg's spotted design bares a strong resemblance to the eggs Yoshi lays in the Super Mario series.
* The egg can hatch into a wikipedia; this is not completely out-of-pocket, since wikipedia exist, but the mammal in question is not one of those.

name: Fernsehbot
description: Its commands restrict the actions of its enemies.
wikiBehavior:
On each of its turns, displays an order. Orders last until its next turn or when it takes damage. Orders include:
* STOP: Cats cannot use their basic movement actions.
* OBEY: Cats cannot use their basic attack or weapons.
* DUMB: Cats cannot use abilities.
* DIE: When the only enemies remaining are Fernsehbots, it will apply Doom to all units on stage, causing them to die after they take their turn.

Fernsehbots also take an additional 2 knockback from attacks.
wikiTrivia:
* The Fernsehbot is a reference to They Live, a 1988 film where most media is revealed to contain subliminal commands.
* "Fernseher" means TV in German.
* The item [[item:TV]] visually resembles this enemy.
* The game's code has 2 additional, unimplemented, abilities:
** "Shit"
** "Fuck"
dangerFlag: Issues orders that disable cat actions (no move / no attack / no abilities). Issues Doom when alone.

name: Fetus
description: Ranged attacker. Can drink water to heal.
wikiBehavior:
* Starts battle at 2/3 hp.
* It uses ranged el shots. 
* Can drink from water tiles to heal. 
* Usually starts the battle in a water tile.
wikiTrivia: The event describes a Mega Fetus as the mother of a Fetus, implying that Fetuses are a species and not unborn human offspring.
categories: Movement keep distance always move prefer water

name: Fetus Gusher
description: Its water attack hits all units in a straight line. Must be in water to attack. Seeks water when out of water.
attackStyle: Ranged piercing attack, Infinite Range Knockback 10
wikiBehavior: Its water attack hits all units in a straight line. Must be in water to attack. Its attacks have knockback.

name: Fetus Gusher (Familiar)
description: Its water attack pushes all units in a straight line. Must be in water to attack. Seeks water when out of water.

name: Flea
description: Its melee attack damages itself.
wikiBehavior: * On their turn, Fleas will attempt to move within melee range of a target and attack it, dealing 4 damage to both them and itself, regardless of the Flea's actual [[stat:STR]]. This self-damage typically kills the Flea.
wikiTrivia:
Fleas are among a small set of enemies that can be spawned as familiars directly.
* Fleas spawned from Cat Abilities will be green.

name: Flesh Golem (Familiar)
wikiBehavior: Flesh Golem is player controlled and will have 1 random spell from each player.
wikiTrivia:
* The Flesh Golem is a reference to  Frankenstein's monster, a living thing made from the flesh of others. (Those "others" are already dead in most versions, however.)
** Its name may be a reference to the Golem in Jewish folklore, as an "incomplete" lifeform made from nonliving matter. Every edition of Dungeons & Dragons has had Flesh Golems, however, so the reference is likely indirect or second-hand.

name: Flesh Lad
description: Attacks as many times as it can, then uppercuts and inflicts Bruise. Gains an extra attack per turn each time it takes damage. Gains Speed at the end of its turn.
wikiBehavior: Gains an attack per turn, and [[status:Health Regen]], each time it takes damage. Gains +1 [[stat:SPD]] each turn.
wikiTrivia:
* Reference to Edmund McMillen's (creator of Mewgenics) other game: [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Meat_Boy|Super Meat Boy]] developed and published by American indie studio Team Meat. 
** Flesh Lad is a comical remix of the main character Meat Boy.
* The vessels on Flesh Lad’s head make it resemble a human heart, complemented by the one-two rhythm of each of his attack, just like a pumping heart.

name: Fleshy Mind
description: Has a ranged attack that inflicts Muted. Inflicts Confusion on units that attack it.
wikiBehavior:
Fleshy Mind will keep distance from it's enemies, and will always try to move to stay in range to attack.
Uses a lobbed Magic attack on all of its enemies within a 3-tile radius. This attack inflicts [[status:Muted]], which doesn't go away until the applier is downed. 
Counterattacks against Melee attacks by applying 1-to-2 [[status:Confusion]].
wikiTrivia:
* They look similar to the Throbbing King.
** They also ressemble fleshy Brain Drain in the way they use ranged magic, share big heads, and jam spells.
dangerFlag: Lobbed attack inflicts Muted on ALL enemies in range. Muted persists until the Fleshy Mind is downed.

name: Floast
description: Has a melee throw attack and a ranged hook attack.
wikiBehavior: The Floast has two attacks, one ranged and one melee. The ranged attack is a linear attack that drags enemies to it, similar to [[item:Meat Hook]]. Its melee attack, "Maul", deals 7 damage and throws its target away from it. If there aren't any targets in range for either attack, it will instead summon a Fly at range 3.
wikiTrivia:
* The Floast is based on an enemy from [[url:https://theendisnigh.fandom.com/wiki/Enemies#Floast/X-Floast|The End is Nigh]].
** Floast also appeared in The Binding of Isaac as a variant of the tboi enemy.

name: Floater
description: Melee Attacker that moves away after it deals damage.
wikiBehavior: Attacks at melee range, then moves away.
wikiTrivia: * Floater is a slang word referring to excrements that float on the water's surface instead of sinking.

name: Florb
description: Its ranged attack inflicts Slow.   Flying.
wikiBehavior:
Takes 1 turn per round. 
Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia: * The Florb is seemingly a seriously progressed instance of the mutations that plague the various cultists in the [[chapter:Bunker]].

name: Florian the Flea
description: Your flea friend till the end!
wikiBehavior: It is a variant of Flea, with the same behavior, but its attack doesn't remove its health.
wikiTrivia: * Florian's name may allude to wikipedia, a developer who made The Binding of Isaac with Edmund McMillen.

name: Fly
description: Melee Attacker. Flying.
wikiBehavior:
* Attacks enemies in melee range.
* Has permament [[status:Flying]].
* Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia: * Flies bear a similar appearance to those found in The Binding of Isaac.

name: Fly Swarm
description: Performs a melee attack that hits once for each fly.   Each time it's damaged it loses a fly.
wikiBehavior:
Attacks once for each fly present, and loses a fly for each health lost.This is not consistent with champion fly swarms.

Can only take 1 damage at a time, but crits can still deal 2 (or 3 with passives like [[ability:Critical]]), similiar to rocks.

name: Fötusjar
description: Multi-hit melee attacker.
wikiBehavior:
A Fötusjar begins with [[status:Brace]] and is immune to all Magic Damage types. It is also immune to all status effects. 

Its main attack is similar to [[ability:Fury Swipes]], in that it has a chance to attack again after each strike, generally resulting in a combo of ~2-5 hits for Physical Damage each.

When killed, the jar will break, and Der Fötus inside will be freed from the jar. A [[obj:Water]] will be created at its position, and all tiles adjacent to it will become [[obj:Glass]].
wikiTrivia:
* The enemy's design may be a reference to the Character Dr. Fetus, the antagonist of [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Meat_Boy|Super Meat Boy]], one of Edmund McMillen's previous games.
** Der Fötus's ability to call down an airstrike may also be a reference to Dr. Fetus.
* Internally, the enemy is named "Fetus Jar".
* "Fötusjar" isn't a correct translation, it would actually be "fötusglas."

name: Frank (Enemy)
description: Will suck units in, then spit them out.
wikiBehavior: Will suck units in, then spit them out. Becomes Frank's Bean when killed.

name: Frank's Bean
description: Melee attacker.
wikiBehavior: Melee attacker. It's behaviour is identical to Pinky, moving randomly and attacking in melee range. It differs in it's increased health and 5 starting [[status:Brace]].
wikiTrivia: * This enemy also appears as the [[item:Extra Set of Eyes]].

name: Frog
wikiBehavior:
Can be summoned via the we weather. Has a hook attack that pulls units in.

They always view bugs (like Fly) as enemies.

name: Führerclone
description: Has a multi-hit melee attack.   Follows orders.
wikiBehavior: Will prioritize attacking enemy units within movement range. If no enemies can be reached, will lick the floor to self heal and clear debuffs.
wikiTrivia:
* Führerclones having exactly 33 HP could be a reference to 1933, the year Adolf Hitler was appointed Chancellor of Germany.
* Due to the hair and the champion variant's Swastika, the turn order icon appears to be flipped.
* Due to sprite flipping Führerclones can salute incorrectly as they are salute with their left hand without anything physically preventing them from saluting with their right.

name: Führerfötus
description: Has a multi-hit melee attack. Follows orders.
wikiBehavior:
Unlike Der Fötus, Führerfötus will not call in airstrikes at low HP. Two random fetuses grow into Führerclone when Hitler II takes an action, and will be healed to 33 HP. 
* This growth effect can even occur on fetuses converted to allies via [[status:Captured Familiar]] or [[ability:Reanimate]].
wikiTrivia: * This enemy's name is a compound word comprising of Führer, a German word meaning "Leader", and often associated with Adolf Hitler's position as leader of Germany, and Fötus, a German word meaning fetus.

name: Fuzzer
description: Melee attacker that inflicts Confusion, then runs away.  Units that contact this get confusion.  Heals whenever an enemy damages itself in confusion.
wikiBehavior:
Inflicts [[status:Confusion]] on units that contact it. Heals when units damage themselves in [[status:Confusion]].

Fuzzers take a bunch of extra Knockback when hit in , but do not take knockback damage.
wikiTrivia:
* It resembles a Tribble from Star Trek: The Original Series.
** Its eyes and Confusion effect better resemble the Fuzzies from Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island.

name: G-Alien
description: "Its ranged attack has knockback. Primes a counterspell at the end of its turn. Is powered up when counterspell is primed."
wikiBehavior: Has counter spell. Can give allies extra turns. Explodes in a 3x3 when killed when it has counterspell available. If it already has a counterspell primed when it's turn starts it knocks back and inflicts [[status:Confusion]] to every enemy in it's line of sight.
wikiTrivia: * G-Aliens are likely a reference to the "[[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey_alien|grey alien]]" trope.

name: Gamete
description: Spawns random units.
wikiBehavior:
Spends a turn to inflate. On its next turn, spawns a random enemy. 
It will attempt to run away from enemy units on the inflating turn, and run towards them before spawning. 
If killed while inflated, bursts like a balloon, applying 2 knockback and the Wind element to adjacent units (and the Tiles they're on). 
Gamete can spawn one of several enemies from [[chapter:Alley]]:
* Mangy
* Lil' Rat
* Leaper
* Pooter
* Kitten
* Tom Tom
* Cat Caller
Champion Gamete spawns champion units. 
Leaves a corpse if killed in flaccid state, not if killed when inflated.
wikiTrivia:
* A  Gamete is a "germ cell", such as a male's sperm or a female's egg. 
* The tails on these Gametes are based on the tails on sperm.
* Very rarely, a "Big" Gamete can be seen behind Stacy in the opening cutscene.

name: Gasper
description: Creates Poison clouds when it attacks or is damaged. Primes an explosion when killed.
wikiBehavior: Flying enemy. Spews poison gas onto the surrounding 4 tiles when it attacks. When it dies, refills its health bar and explodes into more poison gas on its next turn, killing itself. Is poison immune. The explosions destroy static objects.
wikiTrivia:
* Gasper is based on an enemy from [[url:https://theendisnigh.fandom.com/wiki/Enemies#Gasper|The End is Nigh]].
* Its design and poison-gas abilities could be a reference to the Pokemon Koffing.
dangerFlag: Spews poison gas on surrounding tiles. Explodes into more poison gas on death.

name: Gassy (Enemy)
description: Its melee fart inflicts Poison 3. Farts and projects itself forward 3 tiles when damaged.
attackStyle: Melee attack, Poison 3 Dashes 3 tiles away
wikiBehavior:
* Turns itself away from the enemy it attacks.
* Attacks units by farting on them, which inflicts [[status:Poison]] and pushes itself forward 3 tiles.
** Also performs this attack when damaged.
* Is willing to damage its allies if it can attack an enemy as well.

name: Gatekeeper
description: Goes after the cat with the lowest max health. Sucks the soul out of its target, instantly killing it and permanently lowering their Constitution by 2. Summons Skeletons. Undead.
wikiBehavior:
* Performs a melee attack that instantly downs its target and permanently reduces its [[stat:CON]] by 2.
** The Gatekeeper gains [[status:Constitution Up]] and heals Heal health.
* If they cannot reach a target with their regular movement, it will instead perform an infinite-range jump towards a valid target, similar to the mb.
** They cannot perform their melee attack after this jump.
* Will summon skeleton-type enemies to attack its enemies (i.e., Skeleton Cat Bone Worm)
* Prioritizes targeting the allied cat with the lowest health if there are no valid targets in range.
* Starts with [[status:Brace]].
* Classified as undead.
wikiTrivia:
* Based on the fact they're a heavenly gatekeeper, it's possible that the gatekeeper might be based on Saint Peter, the gatekeeper of Heaven and one of Jesus Christ's 12 apostles.
* The cattle skulls on Gatekeepers are possibly a reference to the Chayyoth, or "[[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living_creatures_(Bible)|living creatures]]"; high-ranking angels described in Ezekiel 1 as having human forms, but also an ox's face and hooves. The "living creatures" also have a human face, a lion's face opposite of the ox's face, and an eagle's face.
** The undeath aspect of Gatekeepers might be another reference to Ezekiel; specifically Ezekiel 37, where the prophet has [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vision_of_the_Valley_of_Dry_Bones|a vision of dry skeletons being resurrected]].
* That cats technically survive the Gatekeepers eating their souls might be a reference to Paradise Lost, in which a fallen angel states that only God can properly "annihilate" one.
* A gigantic Gatekeeper can be seen in one of the event backgrounds for [[chapter:The Infinite]], while another appears along the border of one of its arenas.
dangerFlag: Melee attack insta-downs its target and permanently reduces CON by 2.

name: GeoLad
description: Performs a jump attack that damages and knocks back all units in an area.
wikiBehavior:
Has [[status:Brace]]. 
Can move and do the jump attack, damaging and knocking back everyone in ? tile radius from targeted spot. 
When starting turn adjacent to enemy, can do a melee attack that can inflict [[status:Stun]]. 
Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia:
* GeoLad's name is likely a play on the Pokémon [[url:https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Geodude_(Pok%C3%A9mon)|Geodude.]]
** Furthermore, its champion form having a lighter coloration and pronounced, blocky eyebrows is potentially a reference to Alolan Geodude, a seperate form of Geodude.

name: Glass Spitter
description: Its ranged attack spawns glass and inflicts Bleed.
wikiBehavior:
Glass Spitters move to maintain a max range between them and the unit they intent to attack.  

Their attack shoots two lobbed projectiles, landing in a cross shape and applying 1 [[status:Bleed]] on hit and creating [[obj:Glass]] on the tiles they hit. 
* The projectiles can land in any of the 5 spaces in the cross, and as such are not very accurate.
wikiTrivia: * They use a male8 voice for cats, voiced by Cody Glaiel.

name: Glowing Mushroom
description: Grants Mana to nearby units on its turn.
wikiBehavior: Glowing Mushroom is stationary and cannot attack.

name: Golem
description: Invulnerable. Dies when all of its allies are dead.
wikiBehavior:
Flesh Golem Cannot die until all its allies are killed.

Will attempt to walk to his enemies and hit them with a melee attack that deals 2 knockback.

Has 10 initiative.
wikiTrivia:
* Its name may be a reference to the Golem in Jewish folklore, as an "incomplete" lifeform made from nonliving matter. Every edition of Dungeons & Dragons has had Flesh Golems, however, so the reference is likely indirect or second-hand.
* Potentially the same Golem that appears in the event
* Shares its visuals with Flesh Golem.

name: Gorger
description: Its melee attack consumes what it hits.
wikiBehavior: Attempts to consume a cat on its turn, moving up to 1 tile to do so. If there are no cats within 1 tile, automatically moves up to 5 tiles towards a cat at the end of the turn.
wikiTrivia:
* Gorger is based on an enemy from [[url:https://theendisnigh.fandom.com/wiki/Enemies#Gorger|The End is Nigh]], wherein they take on a more sluglike appearance.
* Unlike other instant kill enemies, it's damage does not show as ∞.
* Gorger is the only non-boss enemy that takes up a 3x3 space

name: Grave Worm
description: Ranged attacker. Digs away when damaged.
wikiBehavior: Is a ranged attacker. Burrows to move, and as such doesn't trigger tile movement triggers (like bear trap). Burrows away when attacked. Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia: * They resemble Pin from The Binding Of Isaac.

name: Großerbot
description: Its Suplex attack Stun or Immobilize.  Primes Airstrikes.
wikiBehavior:
Großerbot willl move towards its enemy and perform one of two actions depending on if it's close to the enemy or not.
* Blitzkrieg: Großerbot will prime an airstrike on the enemy if it's too far away, highlighting a 2 tile radius area where it's aiming. The attack will be launched on its next turn.
* Suplex: If Großerbot is adjacent to its enemy, it will suplex them, grabbing and slamming them on the tile behind itself, inflicting [[status:Stun]] or [[status:Immobile]].
wikiTrivia:
* Its Blitzkrieg attack is named after the infamous Nazi military tactic used in World War 2.
* Its Suplex attack is likely based on a popular suplex technique often called the German suplex.
* The "ß" in this enemy's name is the German letter "Eszett" (literally "S-Z"), used for a long "S" sound.
* "Großer" means "big" in German.

name: Half-Dog
description: Has a leap attack with Knockback.
wikiBehavior:
Takes 2 turns per round. 
Has a jump attack with knockback. This leap attack can only target tiles exactly 2 tiles away from the Half-Dog. 
Will jump forward when damaged. This reactive jump is same as attacking one. 
Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia:
* The Half-Dog shares the body of Nubs.
* Champion Half-Dog's death animation still features a non-champion-colored head, as it uses a different head sprite that has no Champion variant.
dangerFlag: Takes 2 turns per round. Leap attack triggers reactively when damaged.

name: Half-Human δ
description: Has a spin attack with knockback.
wikiBehavior:
* Initially has a 25% to dodge attacks from its non-human side.
* In its initial form, has a melee attack that deals 5 damage with 1 knockback and inflicts [[status:Immobile]].
* When it receives fatal damage for the first time it fully recovers its HP, its human half dies, debuffing it with [[status:Movement Down]], and its attack changes to an AOE spin around itself that deals 5 damage with 5 knockback.
wikiTrivia:
* A Half-Human δ is the first Lab creature to attack NPC, following an earthquake that happens after the player clears [[chapter:The Core]] and [[chapter:The Moon]].
* Considering how small the human half of the Half-Human δ is, they might possibly be a young child or toddler, considering how they're approximately the same size as a cat.

name: Half-Rat
description: Does a chaining dash attack.
wikiBehavior:
Has a chain dash attack with range 10 in cardinal directions. 
* Will randomly make another dash attack to the left or right of where the rat is facing if the previous dash attack dealt damage. 
* This attack has a 10% chance to inflict a Disease Disorder on units hit.
The AI does not move in such a way that it takes full advantage of the dash attack for movement purposes, meaning it'll often not attack on its turn.

name: Hängenbot
description: Its melee attack inflicts Short Circuit.  Retracts when damaged.  Spawnes Invaders
wikiBehavior: Applies energized to friendly robots. Applies [[status:Short Circuit]] to the cats that replaces all their abilities with [[ability:Break Circuit]]. One stack of Short Circuit is cleared upon using Break Circuit. Can leave the battlefield and become untargettable until its next turn when hit.
wikiTrivia: * Its level editor sprite is a reference to wikipedia, from the Portal series.

name: Harpy
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up and finds a bonus item!
wikiBehavior: Harpies apply [[status:Fear]] to units that they attack.
wikiTrivia: * A [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harpy|harpy]] is a mythical bird with the head of a woman.

name: Headless
description: Has a spin attack. Shoots a Poison shot when damaged. Blind.
wikiBehavior:
* At the start of its turn, it will move, and then perform it's basic attack. 
** Instead of always trying to approach its enemies, it may move to a random tile. 
* Its basic attack hits every unit around it. 
* When damaged, it shoots a projectile in the direction it's facing. This projectile deals damage and inflicts [[status:Poison]] onto units it hits. 
** This does not happen if the damage was fatal.
* Spawned by the Rock Head enemy upon its defeat.

name: Hell Hand
description: Grapples its enemies if they walk past it.
wikiBehavior:
* Immobile. 
* Interrupts movement and grapples non-allied units that try to move next to it. 
* A Hell Hand can grapple only one unit at time. But one unit can be grabbed by more than one Hell Hand at once.  
* Does not leave a corpse. Not required to kill in order to finish the battle.
wikiTrivia: * It is one of the few enemies in the game to have a champion variant identical to its regular version.

name: Hemlock
description: Attacks units that move in range. Knocks back adjacent units when damaged. Heals allies.
wikiBehavior:
Prefers to stay away from its enemies, avoiding combat. 
Attacks units that end movement in its attack range (3 for basic version), inflicting [[status:Poison]]. 
Knocks back adjacent units when damaged. 
Mainly heals adjacent allies (3 heal waves, restoring 1 HP each). This action does not heal its user. 
Being a support unit by nature, runs from battle when no more combat-oriented allies remain. 
Immune to [[status:Poison]].
wikiTrivia: * Hemlock shares a few visual similarities to the protagonist of Coil, a previous game by Edmund in the Basement Collection.

name: Herald
description: Melee attacker that summons shadows of itself.

name: Heraldess
description: Melee attacker. Becomes scary when damaged.
wikiBehavior: Has a melee attack with knockback that inflicts [[status:Bleed]] 1. When attacked she inflicts [[status:Fear]] on every unit in a 2 tile radius.

name: Horny Cat
description: Its ranged attack inflicts Blind.
wikiBehavior: Has a ranged attack that inflicts [[status:Blind]].
wikiTrivia: * Horny Cats appear to be a reference to [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horned_lizard|horned lizards]], who live in the desert and blind predators by squirting blood from their eyes. Their blood is poisonous to cats and canines, though not to most predatory birds.

name: Host (Enemy)
description: Shoots 3 projectiles in a spread. Reflects projectiles and knocks back units who contact it Stationary.
attackStyle: Ranged attack, Infinite Range Shoots a projectile in a cardinal direction and the two adjacent diagonals.
wikiBehavior: Reflects projectiles shot at it back to sender. Shoots 3 projectiles forward and diagonally of its front when attacking. Knocks back melee attackers at its front. Takes 2 damage from any ranged attacks, no matter the damage the ranged attack normally deals. Will shoot allies as collateral if it can hit an enemy at the same time. Will reflect Butcher's hook, as if it used the hook itself and pulling the Butcher towards it.
wikiTrivia: * Hosts originated from a multiplayer flash game created by Edmund McMillen called HOST. An enemy with the same name also appears in The Binding of Isaac, where they have the same attack pattern as in Mewgenics.
dangerFlag: Reflects all projectiles back at the attacker. Knocks back melee attackers at front.

name: Hot Poker
description: Has 2 melee attacks, one with Immobilize, the other with burn that knocks a unit in the direction it's facing. Can give its allies extra turns. Immune to Fire.
wikiBehavior:
Is immune to el. 
Gets 2 turns per round. Can perform 2 "move and attack" sequences in single turn, just like Werecat. 
Has 3 different melee attacks:
* One melee attack inflicts [[status:Immobile]], and refreshes the user's movement action if it hits.
* a second melee attack does only Physical Damage, but also inflicts [[status:Burn]] and applies 10 Knockback. (This is a el attack.)
* The third does only Physical Damage, gives [[status:Burn]], and has the target take an extra turn immediately after this one. (This is not a el attack.)
Hot Pokers will only use the third attack on their allies.
wikiTrivia:
* The Hot Poker has an "AlwaysHitDifferentTargets" passive, which prevents it from targeting the same unit twice in a round.
** This was possibly put in place to prevent two Hot Pokers from spamming extra turns on each other, which would drastically reduce their [[stat:HEALTH]] and waste the player's time.
dangerFlag: Gets 2 turns per round with 2 move+attack sequences each. Three different melee attacks.

name: Hummingbird
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up and finds a bonus item!
wikiBehavior:
Like all bonus birds, the Hummingbird is a neutral enemy that does not attack the player's cats or the enemies. 

It will flee the battle at the end of its first turn.
wikiTrivia: * Hummingbirds are a family of bird characterized by their small size and extremely fast metabolism. They flap their wings anywhere from 12 to 99 times a second, which produces a bug-like buzzing or humming sound.

name: Husk
description: Has a multi-hit melee attack. Turns into an Edema when killed.
wikiBehavior: Has a multi-hit melee attack. Turns into an Edema when killed.
wikiTrivia: * A Husk appears in the cutscene for unlocking [[chapter:The End]].

name: Hyde
description: Its melee attack can hit multiple times!
wikiBehavior: Its attack is 3x? (4x? for the harder variant), meaning it can attack a random amount of times in one turn and has a [[stat:SPD]] of 4 (5 for the harder variant).
wikiTrivia:
* Hyde's name and mechanic of transforming are an allusion to the 1886 gothic novella Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, that centers around the titular Dr. Jekyll and his transformations into Mr. Hyde.
* Hyde bears a resemblance to Baphomet, an occult goat figure that commonly represents the Devil.
* They use a 0.9 pitch male9 voice, voiced by Cody Glaiel.
dangerFlag: Attacks 3-4 times per turn with high speed. Jekyll transforms into this after 3 turns.

name: Infested (Enemy)
description: Its ranged attack has a chance to break equipment and attach a parasite.
wikiBehavior:
* Fires a ranged attack a the closest enemy target. This attack has a chance to destroy a random piece of held equipment and replace it with a parasite.

* When killed, spawns a Gamete.

name: Infested Kitten
description: Its melee attack inflicts Possessed. Moves away when damaged.
wikiBehavior:
Its melee attack inflicts [[status:Possessed]].
Moves away when damaged.
wikiTrivia: * Likely inspired by Cordyceps, a genus of entomorphopathic fungi. There is brief mention of a mind-controlling fungus infection in Feline Invader, lending credibility to the theory. A similar trope can be seen in media such as The Last of Us and The Girl With All The Gifts.

name: Jack
description: Protects his allies.
wikiBehavior: Protects his allies. Has attack that gives allies in an area 5 shield.
wikiTrivia: * Jack is fully voiced, while NPC is not. It uses a pitched female30 voice for cats, voiced by Peach McMillen.

name: Jekyll
description: It will evolve in several turns.
wikiBehavior:
Spawns with a 3 turn timer. At the end of its 3 turns, it will mutate into a Hyde enemy.
