The Jekyll runs away as far as possible from any enemies. It will only attack and approach an enemy if it can't get farther away.
wikiTrivia:
* Jekyll's name and mechanic of transforming are an allusion to the 1886 gothic novella  Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, that centers around the titular Dr. Jekyll and his transformations into Mr. Hyde.
* They use a 1.5 pitch male7 voice for cats, voiced by Viggo Bossi.

name: Katzebot
description: Melee attacker. Focuses its lowest health enemy. Will Suplex others out of the way.
wikiBehavior: Prioritizes your cat with the least health. Suplexes units in the way of its main target.
wikiTrivia: * Katze means cat in german.

name: Killdozer
description: Moves towards what damages it. Trample.
wikiBehavior:
Starts with 2 [[status:Brace]] and 3 [[status:Thorns]]. Can [[status:Trample]]. 
Moves one tile towards units that damage it, like the Boris boss. 
When reaching enemy on its own turn, performs a very damaging "Killdoze" attack on 2x2 area in front of it. 
Is a Robot.
wikiTrivia: * Killdozer's name and design are based on the real life tank-like bulldozer built by [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Heemeyer|Marvin Heemeyer]], known for the Killdozer rampage incident.

name: Kitten
description: Runs away when damaged.
wikiBehavior:
Moves within melee range of an enemy unit (if necessary) and attacks it. 

When hit, runs away from its attacker.
wikiTrivia: * They use a 2.0 pitch female2 voice for cats.

name: Korbee
description: Will suck units in, then spit them out as far away as it can.
attackStyle: Suck attack, Infinite Range Spit attack, Infinite Range
wikiBehavior:
Korbee's main mechanic and main form of attack is by sucking in units and spitting them out in a different direction. Korbee will attempt to approach one of the enemy units. Once it is lined up with its target along a cardinal direction, Korbee will suck in its target, temporarily removing it from the field. 
Korbee can suck in and swallow any sized enemy, including bosses. It can also just not spit out the enemy after swallowing them.This might be specific to certain enemies, or caused by being blocked in, but it at least can happen with Spinneret.
wikiTrivia:
* Korbee's name and method of attack is based on the Nintendo character [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirby_(character)|Kirby]], both sharing the ability to suck in and spit out enemies.
** Korbee's internal name is "Kirby Fetus".

name: Krughead
description: Melee attacker. Gives it's allies extra turns.  Immune to magic and debuffs.
wikiBehavior:
Krughead starts with [[status:Brace]] and is immune to all Magic Damage and status effects. It counterattacks when damaged by melee attackers.

Upon dying, a [[obj:Water]] will be left on its place and all adjacent tiles will become [[obj:Glass]].

* Befehl: Yells at an ally unit adjacent to it, granting it an extra turn.
wikiTrivia:
* Krug is German for "jug", making the Krugheads "jugheads" (idiots).
* Their ID name, "Jarhead", is a nickname for US Marines with the stereotypical army buzzcut.
* The Befehl attack seems to be inspired by Adolf Hitler's infamous viral rant scene "Das war ein Befehl" ("That was an order"), a famous line from the 2004 film Downfall (Der Untergang).

name: Leaper
description: Its leap attack damages and knocks back all adjacent units.
attackStyle: Jump attack, Range 3 Damage, Knockback 1 in Range 1
wikiBehavior: Attempts to move within a moderate distance of the player's units, performing a leap attack that deals its damage to all adjacent (cardinal) units and inflicting knockback. This attack cannot target a space occupied by a unit, unlike other similar abilities.
wikiTrivia: * Leapers, along with Lil' Rats, were one of the very first enemies created, appearing in very early footage of development when the team was still experimenting with the game's playstyle.

name: Leech (Familiar)
description: Melee attacker.
wikiBehavior:
* The Leech has a melee attack with [[status:Lifesteal]]. This Lifesteal also Heal the Leech's owner by the same amount.
* Attacks enemies in melee range.
* Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia: * Leeches are Annelids (like earthworms), belonging to the class Clitellata (also like earthworms) and the subclass Hirudinea.

name: Lil' Rat
description: Dashes in a straight line.
wikiBehavior: Attacks enemies by dashing in a cardinal direction (10 tile range). Will not dash if it cannot hit an enemy with the attack.
wikiTrivia: * Lil' Rats were one of the very first enemies created, even appearing in the very early stages of development when the team was still experimenting with the game's playstyle.

name: Louse
description: Its melee attacks inflict Bruise
wikiTrivia: * Its sprite is just a small Flea.

name: Love Bot
description: Heals and gives +1 Speed to its allies. Its heal can grant an extra turn if healed over max
wikiBehavior:
Has [[status:Brace]] 1. 
Takes 1 turn per round. 
Heals allies or gives them extra turn if they have full health. 
Can retaliate when attacked from adjacent tile, similar to bonus birds. Retaliation hit inflicts debuffs. 
Is a robot and [[status:Energized]] by Electric element. 
Will run if no damage-dealing allies left.
wikiTrivia: The two cube shaped objects on their torso were most likely made to resemble [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast|human breasts]].

name: Lumpy
description: Its ranged attack creates Creep. Spawns Creep when damaged.
wikiBehavior: Has a chance to spawn a creep tile in a 3x3 area around it when damaged. Does not take creep tile damage. Its attacks can spawn creep tiles.

name: Maelestes
description: Steals equipement from cats.  Collects pickups.
wikiBehavior: * Can pick up pickups and steal equipment from cats. The equipment that is stolen is permanently lost.
wikiTrivia:
* In paleontology, Maelestes is a prehistoric shrew-like mammal discovered in 1997 in the Gobi Desert. The animal lived in the late Cretaceous Period, around 71–75 million years ago.
** Despite being the representative mammal for the area, there are no living creatures known to descend from Maelestes; their taxonomic order (Cimolesta) became distinct from other mammals 80 million years ago, and died out 28 million years ago.
** The oldest fossils of mammals (in general) date to the late Jurassic, though mammals are presumed to have evolved earlier in the era.
* Tyler teased this enemy in [[url:https://x.com/TylerGlaiel/status/1796674134279356490?s=20|July 2024]], claiming it "will be your most hated enemy".
dangerFlag: Steals equipment from cats. The stolen equipment is permanently lost.

name: Maggot
description: Melee attacker.
wikiBehavior:
* Attacks enemies in melee range.
* Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia:
* Maggots have a similar appearance to the Worm Trinkets found in The Binding of Isaac.
* Despite being the larval form of Flies, Maggots aren't able to be spawned by them in any way, and don't have the same types.

name: Mammoth Kitten
description: Its melee attack knocks units into the air.  Bruises and knocks back adjacent units at the start of its turn.  Trample.
wikiBehavior:
Bruises and knocks back units at the start of its turn. Has melee attack with knock up. Has trample.
Their bodies take three hits to destroy, and drop a large food pickup when destroyed.

name: Mangy
description: Its ranged attack may inflict Poison. Spawns maggots when damaged.
attackStyle: Lobbed attack, Range 3, chance for Poison 1 Blind spot, Range 1
wikiBehavior:
* Uses a ranged attack that may inflict [[status:Poison]].
* Has a chance to summon a Maggot every time it is hit, save for the hit that kills it.
wikiTrivia:
* They use the male4 voice for cats, voiced by Eryck Lindquist.
* Mangies are part of a small set of enemies that appear in all 3 Acts.

name: Meat Slime
description: Splits into Clots on death.
wikiBehavior: * Splits into multiple Clots upon death.

name: Mech Suit (Familiar)
wikiTrivia: * The [[ability:Mech Suit]] and Thrusters ability tooltips show a round mech design, despite the in-game model being square.

name: Mega Fetus
description: Performs a spin attack. Will try to counterattack with its left arm when hit
wikiBehavior: Does a melee spin attack with knockback. Will attack specific tiles when damaged. Will attack the two tiles in front of its left arm in the direction from which it was attack, with knockback.
wikiTrivia: The event describes a Mega Fetus as the mother of a Fetus, implying that Fetuses are a species and not unborn human offspring.

name: Mega Mutant
description: Melee attacks adjacent units with Knockback 10 at the start of its turn.
wikiBehavior:
Mega Mutants are a large, slow enemy type formidable at both close and long range. Their most dangerous characteristic is their access to Lacerate, a melee-range attack that can instantly down an affected cat.
When attacked, Mega Mutants gain 99 stacks of [[status:Brace]] until the start of their next turn, making them extremely difficult to burst down with multiple attacks. Mega Mutants will also always perform a melee attack against units it begins its turn adjacent to that will knock them away 10 tiles.
wikiTrivia: * If Mega Mutant is given a miss chance, such as through the Blind debuff, it can miss its Lacerate attack, however, the attack animation will still play and the miss text will only occur after the attack animation concludes, with the target being unaffected.
dangerFlag: Lacerate insta-downs any cat it hits. Gains 99 Brace when attacked, making burst damage useless.

name: Mega Tumor
description: Trample.
wikiBehavior:
* [[status:Trample]].
* Gains +1 movement range at the end of its turns.
* Its attack inflicts [[status:Immobile]] and [[status:Bruise]].
wikiTrivia: * Mega Tumors might be a reference to a type of collectible in The End is Nigh, another game by Edmund McMillen and Tyler Glaiel.

name: Megasaucer
description: Performs a random action on its turn. Has a dash attack that inflicts Stun. Has a charge up laser attack that instakills. Has the ability to summon B-Probers. Explodes when killed.
wikiBehavior: Explodes on death. The insta kill laser is two tiles wide.
dangerFlag: Explodes on death. Has a two-tile-wide insta-kill laser.

name: Moon Worm
description: Lobs shots at all of its enemies within range.  Gains +1 Brace when damaged.
wikiBehavior:
* Will burrow towards a target and shoot all enemy units in its attack range with a 1-damage projectile attack after it stops moving.
* Gains [[status:Brace]] every time it takes damage.
wikiTrivia: * This enemy could potentially be a reference to the [[url:https://futurama.fandom.com/wiki/Moon_Worm|Mighty Moon Worm]] from Futurama.

name: Moth
wikiBehavior:
* [[status:Flying]].
* Has 8 [[stat:STR]], 8 [[stat:DEX]], 8 [[stat:CON]], 8 [[stat:SPD]], 8 [[stat:INT]], 8 [[stat:CHA]], and 8 [[stat:LCK]].
* Also has access to [[ability:Flutter]] and [[ability:Sleep Powder]].

name: Mummified Mangy
description: Its ranged attack may inflict Poison.  Spawns Maggots when damaged.  Becomes a Carcass when killed.
wikiBehavior:
Spawns Maggot when damaged. Can [[status:Poison]] with ranged attack. 
Turns into Carcass when downed. Is classified as an undead.

name: Mutant
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up and finds a bonus item!
wikiBehavior: Mutant Birds apply 1 [[status:Bruise]] and 3 knockback to units that they attack.
wikiTrivia:
* For unknown reasons, all the medium bonus birds use the Pigeon's beak for a few frames in its attack animation. This is especially noticeable on the Mutant.
* Mutants are often found in a handful of unused [[chapter:Bunker]] room layouts, which could suggest that they were originally meant to be exclusive to that area.

name: Nettle
description: Gains thorns. Is a melee attacker
wikiBehavior: The Nettle gains [[status:Thorns]] and emits a Sparkle each time an enemy uses a spell (an ability other than a basic attack). On its turn it will move towards an enemy and use a melee attack that inflicts [[status:Bleed]].
wikiTrivia: * Nettles are prickly plants with stinging hairs, particularly from the genus Urtica or those that look like them, some featuring a bulbous seed pod covered in spikes which bursts to catapult their content

name: Nurse Bot (Familiar)
wikiBehavior:
Cannot deal damage, will stay close to allies and attempt to heal them. Will prioritize healing [[type:Cat]].
* Basic attack - Heals allies for 5, scales with [[stat:STR]], cannot heal other robots.
* [[status:Damage Up]] will increase the healing.
wikiTrivia: * Uses the same graphics as Love Bot, but slightly smaller (70% of the size).

name: Parasaurolophus
description: Its attacks always crit against Wet units.  Tries to toss units into water.
wikiBehavior:
Parasauropholus are melee units designed around their unique gimmick of always dealing critical damage to [[status:Wet]] units. They can only appear in arenas with [[obj:Water]], and while they ordinarily have a pitiful 1 [[stat:MOVEMENT RANGE]], this significantly increases when in water.

They have two attacks. Against non-[[status:Wet]] enemies, they will attempt to move close and use a [[ability:Toss]]-like ability to throw them into a body of water. Once their enemies are wet, they have a Physical Damage (Physical Damage on crit) headbutt similar to [[ability:Push Attack]], complete with the 1 knockback and 1 tile of movement.
wikiTrivia: *The genus of dinosaur this enemy is based on actually dates to ~80 million years after the [[chapter:Jurassic]] period.

name: Peashy
description: May attack its own allies.
wikiBehavior:
* Uses a ranged attack in a straight line.
* Has [[status:Thorns]]. 
* Blocks damage from the front. 
* Attacks allies, similar to [[status:Madness]].
* Upon killing a unit, becomes enraged. When enraged, its attack inflicts [[status:Bleed]] 3, and it heals every time it kills something.
** Units that die from a Peashy's thorns counts as a kill for the sake of enraging it.
wikiTrivia:
* Peashy is a direct reference to [[url:https://golgotha.fandom.com/wiki/Cereus_Peashy_(Character)|Cereus Peashy]], a character from earlier games by Edmund McMillen, inclusively starring in his own game of the [[url:https://golgotha.fandom.com/wiki/Cereus_Peashy_(Game)|same name]].
* Peashy's initial reveal in 2022 presented it when the game's color pallete was primarily black and white. Later appearances of it in the years following showcased it with colors added in.
* Peashy's level editor icon, shared by Tyler Glaiel on the official Discord server, is drawn in a way that resembles the Crewmates from the 2018 Indie Game [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Among_Us|Among Us]].
** That might mean its tendency to attack its allies is also a reference to the imposters in the game.
dangerFlag: Blocks damage from the front. Becomes enraged after killing a unit, gaining Bleed 3 on attacks.

name: Pet Boulder
description: Attack it to push it 1 tile. It deals 9 damage to units it hits.
wikiBehavior:
Will slowly move towards enemies, and hit them with 1 knockback when adjacent. 
* Can attack diagonally.
* Immune to Status Effects.
* Can only take 1 damage at a time.
* Will attack last in the round in most cases (-80 initiative).

name: Pet Rock
description: Abilities like Pet Rocks summon Pet Rock.
wikiBehavior:
Pet Rocks attempt to line up with an enemy before performing a dash attack in a straight line.

* Can attack diagonally.
* Will attack last in the round in most cases (-80 initiative).
wikiTrivia: * Pet Rock is a reference to real life Pet Rock collectible toy made in 1975.

name: Phantom Mask (Familiar)
description: Invulnerable. Attack it to knock it foward in a straight line. It deals 5 damage to units it hits.
wikiBehavior:
Will move and attack similarly to Pet Rock:
* Can dash in a straight or diagonal line to hit enemies.
* Will dash forward and deal 5 damage to the first unit it hits when attacked.
wikiTrivia: * The item's description has a typo: "foward" instead of "forward"

name: Pigeon
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up and finds a bonus item!
wikiBehavior:
Pigeons are peaceful enemies with a low chance of appearing when the player enters the level.

Their turns consist of moving to random tiles, they never interact with other units. 

When moving, they ignore hazards such as brambles. 

After 2 turns, Pigeons will leave the combat.

However, if killed prior to flying out, Whoever kills it gains an all stats up and finds a bonus at the end of combat.

name: Pile
description: Its ranged attack spawns Dips. Stationary
attackStyle: Lobbed attack, Range 7 Blindspot, Range 1 Spawns a dip
wikiBehavior:
Cannot move. Has a ranged attack with 7 range that deals 2 damage and spawns a Dip on successful hit. 

If no targets are in range, it will spawn a dip adjacent to it.
wikiTrivia: * Pile comes from the vulgar slang pile of shit.

name: Pinky
description: Melee attacker. Moves randomly.
wikiBehavior:
* Moves to random tiles every turn.
* Attacks an enemy, if it moves next to one.
wikiTrivia:
* Colloquially, a pinky is a newborn rat or mouse.
* A pinky can become a party member during a skill event by charming rats. However, they do not provide much tactical advantage.
** Being Fetus-type enemies, they can also become party members during skill events involving fetuses.

name: Poop Cat
description: Nasty.
wikiBehavior: Poop Cat will try to reach the player's cats and attack them from  range. His attack will do 3 damage and inflict [[status:Poison]] and [[status:Slow]].
wikiTrivia:
* It is overtly implied these cats come from inside the Dreadnoughtus's stomach, either swallowed whole and coated in poop, or living within, eating their poop.
** Could be a reference to the fact some [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrolith|Dinosaurs used to eat rocks]] to help with their digestion.

name: Pooter
description: Ranged Attacker. Flying.
wikiBehavior:
* Lobbed projectile (ranged) attacker.
* Has permanent [[status:Flying]].
wikiTrivia:
* Pooters' name and behavior come from the enemies with the same name from The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth.
** Pooters in that game had two compound eyes, however, while Pooters in this one have only one. 
*** Edmund McMillen stated that this difference in appearance stems from the original design being Issac's interpretation of them in his imagination, whereas the Mewgenics iteration is the "real" version.

name: Popeye
description: Has a dash attack with knockback.
wikiBehavior: Its Dash attack will knock units backwards 10 tiles.
wikiTrivia:
* Inspired by the cartoon character [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popeye|Popeye]], with a similar squinting eye.
* They have a 0.6 pitch male2 voice for cats, voiced by Matthias Bossi of Ridiculon.

name: Prehistoric Pooter
description: Its ranged attack inflicts Stun.  Flying.
wikiBehavior: It’s a Pooter but its attacks stun.

name: Pterodactyl
description: Will pick up cats and peck them. Flying.
wikiBehavior:
* Pterodactyls move towards cats and pick them up. If successful, the pterodactyl's movement will refresh and it will move away from the rest of the cats.
** Pterodactyls will only attempt to pick up the player's cats and certain other cat-type units (e.g. a summoned Tom Tom)
** Will not pick up corpses.
* Held cats will be pecked for 3x2 damage, on subsequent turns.
* Pterodactyls have a 50% chance to drop a held cat when damaged by an attack, throwing them 1-4 tiles away in the direction the Pterodactyl is facing.
* A cat held by a pterodactyl has its basic attack replaced with [[ability:Escape?]], can't use spells and cannot be targeted.
* When downed, any cats being carried by a Pterodactyl will be dropped.
* If attacking a unit other than a cat, a pterodactyl will perform a simple melee attack with no animation (possibly bugged)
wikiTrivia:
* Pterodactylus antiquus (which roughly translates to "vintage winged finger") was a late Jurassic pterosaur, belonging to the first order of vertebrates that could fly under their own power. 
** Pterosaurs were not Dinosaurs, though the two were related. Ironically, Birds evolved from Dinosaurs who could also fly, while Pterosaurs have no living descendants. The fossil record shows bird-like Dinosaurs such as Archaeopteryx already existing in the late Jurassic, though whether or not they could fly is unknown.

name: Raptor
description: Its melee attack hits a random amount of times. Pack hunter.
wikiBehavior:
Raptors have fairly-complex AI. They tend to all target the same cat at a time. They try to move to abnormal tiles, such as [[obj:Tall Grass]] or [[obj:Water]], when approaching. They try to hold back on attacking until the other Raptors are also within attacking range.

They have the standard enemy Fury Swipes:
* It has a base damage of Physical Damage.
* It has a 75% chance to repeat, and can repeat up to 8 times in a row.
They get 2 turns per round.
wikiTrivia:
* "Raptor" is a general term for smaller carnivorous dinosaurs, popularized by the [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velociraptor|Velociraptor's]] portrayal in Jurassic Park.
** While the Jurassic (and even the Triassic) had similar kinds of dinosaurs, the types called "Raptors" all come from the Cretaceous.
** Paleontologists are now fairly certain that "Raptors" had feathers, though these are typically omitted in fiction.
dangerFlag: Fury Swipes with 75% chance to repeat each hit. Packs coordinate to attack together.

name: Raptor Kitten
description: Its melee attack inflicts bleed. Moves far away after attacking.
wikiBehavior: The Raptor Kitten is a standard melee unit that attempts to move in range of a target and attack them, dealing Physical Damage and inflicting [[status:Bleed]]. If they can connect an attack, they recieve an additional movement action that they will use to retreat to safety.

name: Rattlesnek
description: Ambushes enemies who walk past it. Its attacks inflict poison.
wikiBehavior:
Rattlesneks Ambush any enemy of theirs who moves into a tile adjacent to them, interrupting their movement and attacking them.
* Their melee attack inflicts 1 [[status:Poison]], on top of doing damage.
* Fortunately (or unfortunately if you have one as a Familiar), Rattlesneks have a 50% chance to skip their movement action each turn. 

When it moves and attacks enemy directly on its own turn (not as ambush), it can step away one tile afterwards.

Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia: * Rattlesneks have 2 [[stat:CHA]].

name: Raven
description: Whoever kills this gets all stats up and a bonus item!
wikiBehavior:
The Raven is a Bird. It is a true neutral unit; gray on the simplified map, like downed units. It moves by [[status:Flying]].

When attacked, Ravens immediately:
* counterattack, if the attacker is within their melee attack's reach.
* take a movement action to fly away from the attacker.

Ravens will eventually Run from the battle, if they are not slain.
wikiTrivia:
* Ravens are members of the genus Corvus, which also includes Crows.
* Ravens applying the madness status effect might be a reference to the poem of the same name by Edgar Allan Poe.
* For unknown reasons, all the medium bonus birds use the Pigeon's beak for a few frames in its attack animation.

name: Reaper
description: Performs a spin attack at the start of its turn. Teleports to units that kill its allies. Undead.
wikiBehavior:
Does a spin attack at the start of its turn. Teleports adjacent to any unit that defeats its allies, receiving 1 [[status:All Stats Up]] and gaining +4 [[stat:HEALTH]] in the process. Attacks after teleporting (if it teleports), and moves after attacking. 
Can walk through walls. Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia:
* The Reaper’s name and appearance is based on the [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grim%20Reaper|Grim Reaper]], a personification of the concept of Death often seen in western culture.
** Despite representing the concept of death, npc blames The Creator for the death of his kitten instead of the reaper.

name: Robes
description: Its ranged attack inflicts Leech. Can summon Wisps. Becomes a Tatters when killed. Undead.
wikiBehavior: Has ranged attack with infinite range that inflicts leech 1. Turns into [[url:https://mewgenics.wiki.gg/wiki/Tatters/|Tatters]]  on death. Can spawn [[url:https://mewgenics.wiki.gg/wiki/Wisp/|Wisps]].

name: Robo-Cat
description: Its wide melee attacks have Knockback 10
wikiBehavior:
The Robo-Cat is a Robot Cat, who starts with a [[status:Shield]]. It behaves like an Albino Tom Tom and starts with 3 [[status:Brace]].

When hit by Electric-element effects, Robots are [[status:Energized]], receiving an extra turn.

name: Robo-Vac (Familiar)
wikiBehavior:
* Will go around the map and focus on collecting Pickups, sharing the effects with the unit that spawned it.
* Will attack enemies with a dashing melee attack if they are standing on a pickup or if there aren't any pickups left on the map.
wikiTrivia: * This familiar is a reference to the Roomba robot vacuum from the company iRobot, which is confirmed by its internal file name of "roomba."

name: Rock Head
description: Has a spin attack and a dash attack with Trample. Blind.
wikiBehavior:
Typically uses dash as its last action in the round. 
Blocks attacks from the front. 
Counts as rock for related enemies and abilities. 
Separates into a [[obj:Boulder]] and Headless when "killed."

name: Rocket Turret
wikiBehavior: Cannot move, uses a lobbed attack within 6 tile range, that attack deals 5 damage, 1 knockback, el and el.

name: Rot Fly
description: Melee attacker. Flying.

name: Rover
description: Has a chaining dash attack.
wikiTrivia:
* Rover's upper half bares identical to Robo-Cat, implying they are the same robot, only re-tooled for moon exploration.
** Given that Robo-Cat's are robots found in [[chapter:The Lab]], and are thus creations of npc, it can be extrapolated that Rover is also a creation of Dr. Beanies.

name: Sabertooth Cat
description: Pounces on units.  Does a double-hit melee attack that inflicts bleed at the start of its turn if any enemies are adjacent.  Hates Cavemen!
wikiBehavior:
Can pounce on units from a distance and deal damage adjacent to where it lands, If this attack hits a Caveman Man, it has a 50% chance of transforming them to a Wereman.

At the start of its turn, does a double-hit melee attack that inflicts [[status:Bleed]] on each hit to all adjacent targets.
Each hit has a 20% chance to transform cavemen into weremen.

Like other Cat-type enemies in the chapter, the Sabertooth Cat has a hatred of Cavemen-type enemies - and may prioritize attacking them if they are in range.
wikiTrivia: * There were several different species of Sabertooth Cats in the last Ice Age, belonging to the genera  [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smilodon|Smilodon]] and [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homotherium|Homotherium]]. Their latest common ancestor with modern cats existed 20 million years ago.

name: Sabertooth Kitten
description: Has a multi hit melee attack that inflicts Bleed.  Can heal its allies.  Hates Cavemen!
wikiBehavior:
* Has a double hit melee attack that inflicts bleed. 
* Can heal its allies. 
* Will attack cavemen regardless of if it is an ally.
wikiTrivia: * The Sabertooth kitten uses the exact same idle animation as its adult counterpart and the Werecat.

name: Saucie
description: Fires energy shots in an X shape.  Can inflict Marked on enemies or gain Holy Shield. Explodes when killed.
wikiBehavior:
While these enemies deal low amounts of damage, their attacks are relentless and versatile. Saucies get three turns per round (four if a champion).

Their main weakness is their lack of movement range and low amount of health.

These enemies are considered robotic and will be [[status:Energized]] by electric attacks.

* Zorp: Four infinite range projectiles in an X pattern. Hits through terrain and has 1 knockback due to moon gravity. If there are hazards on the map (such as Black Holes or Neutron Stars), Saucies will attempt to push enemies into them with this attack.
* Detect: Debuffs an enemy within a 3 tile range with [[status:Marked]].
* Shields Up: Gains +118x18px|link=Status Effects#Holy Shield

On death, Saucies get knocked upwards and away from the attack direction and explode for 5 damage.
dangerFlag: Gets 3 turns per round (4 as champion). Fires infinite-range projectiles in X pattern.

name: Scary
description: Its melee attacks can inflict Fear or Doom! Undead.
attackStyle: Melee attack Chance to inflict Fear 1 or Doomed 3
wikiBehavior:
Has two different melee attacks; one inflicts [[status:Fear]], while the other inflicts [[status:Doomed]]. Neither attack does damage.

It's a Flying Ghost unit, who moves via teleportation. Being body-less, it dies when downed.

It's one of two enemies that can potentially spawn when a [[obj:Tombstone (Ghost)]] is destroyed, with the other one being the Spookie. This can also happen during the fight with Dybbuk, though (like Dybbuk's spawned units) they will flee if Dybbuk is defeated.
wikiTrivia: * Its name combined with the other ghost enemy, Spookie, is likely a reference to the song [[url:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sVjk5nrb_lI|Spooky Scary Skeletons]].

name: Schpidenbot
description: Melee attacker that inflicts Poison.
wikiTrivia:
* In the descriptions of the Hängenbot and Doktorbot, Schpidenbots are called "Invaders".
** Contrary to this name, they cannot apply [[status:Infested]] (unlike their non-robotic counterpart).
* The name imitates a German-sounding word for "spider bot"; a more accurate translation would be "Spinnenbot", combining the German word for spider with the English word "robot".

name: Schutzbot
description: Ranged attacker with limited ammo.  Shoots at enemies that damage its allies.  Expends the rest of its ammo and reloads at the end of its turn.  Backflips one attack per turn.
wikiBehavior:
The Schutzbot can effectively be considered a stronger version of Cop Bot and its ammo-based reactive attack mechanic. When any of its allies are attacked, it will fire a bullet at the source of the damage by spending [[status:Ammo]] if it has any. It will not react if it itself is attacked.

During its turn, the Schutzbot will first expend any remaining [[status:Ammo]] to perform that many attacks if it can. This attack can be aimed at downed cats, leading to their permanent death. Afterwards, the Schutzbot uses Reload, setting its [[status:Ammo]] to 3 and gaining [[status:Backflip]], the latter of which can stack.
wikiTrivia: * "Schutz" means protection in German, but the name is also a play on the English word "shoots".

name: Scorpion Cat
description: Its melee attacks can Poison or Immobilize.
wikiBehavior:
The Scorpion Cat is a slow melee attacker with two separate attacks. They start with [[status:Brace]] and get two turns per round. 

It can either use a [[status:Grappled]] attack that inflicts [[status:Immobile]] on its target for as long as they are adjacent, or it can use a Sting attack that inflicts [[status:Poison]].
dangerFlag: Two turns per round. Grapples targets with Immobile and Poisons with sting.

name: Seagull
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up and finds a bonus item!
wikiBehavior: Seagulls are peaceful enemies with a low chance of appearing when the player enters the level. Their turns consist of moving to random tiles, they never interact with other units. When moving, they ignore hazards such as brambles. After a few turns, Seagulls will fly out of the level, leaving the combat. However, if killed prior to flying out, Whoever kills it gains an all stats up and finds a bonus item at the end of combat.
wikiTrivia:
* Mewgenics Seagull resembles the [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_herring_gull|European herring gull]], which is not' found in America.
* For unknown reasons, all the medium bonus birds use the Pigeon's beak for a few frames in its attack animation.

name: Security Bot
description: When its allies are damaged, it will move towards the attacker and attempt to attack it. Gains +1 movement range at the end of its turn.
wikiBehavior:
Has [[status:Brace]] 2. When an allied unit is damaged, it will move towards the attacker and attack if it is in range, inflicting [[status:Bleed]].

Like other robot units, Security Bot get's [[status:Energized]] when affected by El elements.

Doesn’t attack on its own turn; instead, charges up, gaining [[status:Movement Up]].

Most of its health comes in the form of [[status:Shield]]. 

If the only enemies left are Security Bots, they will enrage and start attacking on their turns.

name: Seraphim
description: Has a diagonal Holy attack. Can revive its downed allies. Units that contact or attack this get knocked back 5 tiles. Immune to Holy. Gains All Stats Up when struck with Holy Element.
wikiBehavior: A Seraphim will prioritize reviving any of its dead allies. If none of its allies are dead or it can't reach any allied bodies, it will try to hit the player's cats with an infinite range el attack that hits all tiles diagonal to it.
wikiTrivia:
* Seraphim, along with The Creator, have no face. This is in reference to Exodus 33:20 in the Bible, when God stated: "But," He said, "you cannot see my face, for man shall not see me and live."
** Despite having no face, when Seraphim die, everything but their wings are vaporized in a beam of holy light. In this beam of light, the imprint of a distraught face can be made out.
* Seraphim bear a resemblance to the angel mini-bosses from The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth. The normal variant resembles Uriel, while the Champion resembles Gabriel.
* This enemy is based on the Abrahamic religion creature  [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seraph|of the same name]].
dangerFlag: Revives dead allies. Has infinite-range diagonal attack.

name: Shade Cat
description: Melee attacker. Teleports behind a random one of its enemies when damaged.
wikiBehavior: Its melee attack always causes units to flee, similar to how kittens do.
wikiTips:
* Cover the backs of your allies to lower the potential spots it can appear in. This can also be used to trick them into teleporting into traps or a melee attack's range.
* [[status:Charmed]] it will cause it to teleport behind its allies, as though it was on the player's team.

name: Shambler
description: Will throw units it can reach. Lunges in a random direction at the end of its turn. Undead
wikiBehavior:
Will move towards its enemies, has [[status:Trample]].

Has a spell that tosses a unit 5-8 tiles away, dealing 5 damage.
* Damage scales with [[stat:STR]]
At the end of its turn, dashes 2 tiles in a random direction, dealing 5 damage and 1 knockback.
* Damage scales with [[stat:STR]]
wikiTrivia: * A Shambler is one of the enemies that can appear in the opening cutscene, specifically left of Edmund's gravestone.

name: Sharky
description: Its bite inflicts Bleed. Takes bonus turns for each bleeding unit. Focuses on bleeding units
wikiBehavior:
The Sharky is a melee attacker that attempts to get close to use a lunging melee attack that deals 2 damage and inflicts [[status:Bleed]].

Additionally, like the other [[type:Shark]] units, it both gains an extra turn for every [[status:Bleed]] unit and will target said units with priority, regardless of if they are enemies or not.

name: Siren
description: Calls its enemies towards it and heals its adjacent allies.
wikiBehavior: Moves near hazards and/or its allies before attempting to lure one of its enemies into a vulnerable position.
wikiTrivia:
* In Greek mythology, [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siren%20(mythology)|sirens]] are creatures, often depicted as having an upper body of a beautiful woman and a lower body of a bird, that lure sailors to their death with their powerful singing voices.
** The behavior of the Siren in-game directly mirrors its mythological counterpart. Its ears also resemble the wings of a bird, with its face having exaggerated feminine features.
* Siren look and behave similar to Cat Caller.
* They use a 0.7 pitch female10 voice for cats.

name: Skeleton Cat
description: Comes back from the dead if its body isn't destroyed! Undead.
wikiBehavior:
The Skeleton Cat is a standard melee unit. It attempts to move towards an enemy to hit them with a melee attack for 9 damage.

In their base form they only have one point of [[status:Shield]] for health, however when they are downed they do not immediately die, rather they convert to a "corpse" state with much more health. If not destroyed by its next turn, the corpse will revive itself and it will return to its base form.

This is an undead unit, meaning it takes damage from Holy element attacks and spells, including healing spells.
wikiTrivia: * They are likely a reference to the [[url:https://www.mariowiki.com/Dry_Bones|Dry Bones]] from the Super Mario franchise, as both are skeletal enemies with the ability to revive after being initially defeated.
dangerFlag: Revives itself after being downed unless the corpse is destroyed.

name: Skeleton Kitten
wikiBehavior:
Will attempt to melee attack enemies.

When downed they gain 6 shield, status immunity and will revive after 1 turn.
dangerFlag: Gains 6 Shield and status immunity when downed. Revives after 1 turn.

name: Skeleton Shambler
description: Will throw units it can reach.
wikiBehavior:
Will move toward any unit it can reach and throw it at player's cats. 
Lunges in a random direction at the end of its turn. 
Comes back from the dead on its next turn (with its full amount of Shield) if its body isn't destroyed. 
Undead.

name: Skinned
description: Does 3 dash attacks in a row with Knockback.
wikiBehavior: Melee attacker with a dash attack that hits three times. Gains [[status:Bleed]] each time it takes damage.
wikiTrivia: * Potentially a reference to the [[url:https://www.wikiraider.com/index.php/Atlanteans|Atlantean]] creatures from Tomb Raider.

name: Skull Ooze
description: Its ranged attack destroys equipment.
attackStyle: Ranged attack, Range 2 Destroys equipment Inflicts Burn 2
wikiBehavior: 5 Damage Ranged Attack that Destroys Equipment, 2 Tile range.
dangerFlag: Ranged attack destroys equipped items.

name: Slag
description: "Does a ranged area attack. Spawns Edemas when damaged by a melee attack and Fly Swarms when damaged by a ranged attack."
wikiBehavior: Spawns Edemas when damaged by a melee attack and Fly Swarms when damaged by a ranged attack. Does not summon when damaged by status effects. Shoots multiple bones at an area which cause bruise.
wikiTrivia:
* The Slag is based on an enemy from [[url:https://theendisnigh.fandom.com/wiki/Slags|The End is Nigh]].
* The Slag appears to be a discolored Mega Tumor with added bones.

name: Sleep Paralysis Demon
description: When killed, the afflicted cat wakes up.
wikiBehavior: Will attack like Hyde.
wikiTrivia: * Many people who suffer from  Sleep Paralysis report hallucinations, such as an intruding presence or dark figure in the room, commonly known as demons.

name: Small Asteroid
description: Its attack shoots rocks at random tiles in an area. Gets knocked back with Chain Knockback when hit. Can only receive 1 damage at a time. Immune to status effects.
wikiBehavior:
* Floats. Immune to status effects. 
* Attacks by spitting 3 [[obj:Small Rock]] within fairly large targeting area, making it very inaccurate and inconsistent at actually dealing damage, but may eventually harm something once enough rocks are littered around the ground and bounce off each other. 
* Has chain knockback when damaged. Can only take one damage at a time (2 if critical hit).

name: Snake
wikiBehavior: Melee attacker, inflicts [[status:Poison]].
wikiTrivia: * Snakes are mostly identical to Rattlesneks, though they lack the ambush attack and have less health.

name: Spider Cat
description: Its melee attack has Lifesteal. Will move away after it attacks. Immune to tile effects.
wikiBehavior: Starts battle at half HP. Hit-and-run attacker. Gets a second movement action after attack, which it uses to keep safe distance from enemies. Likes doing backstabs. Leeches HP on attack (same amount as HP damage done).

name: Spider Kitten
description: Will web units, then drain their HP Immune to Webs.
attackStyle: Lobbed attack, 3 Range Inflicts Webbed 1 Melee attack, Lifesteal
wikiBehavior: Starts the battle at half health. Has a lobbed non damaging ranged attack that inflicts [[status:Webbed]], and a melee attack with lifedrain. Immune to webs. Will first try to [[status:Webbed]] cats, before using its melee attack on webbed cats.
wikiTrivia:
* Spider Kittens are not immune to [[status:Webbed]] itself; they're just immune to [[obj:Web]].
** The best way to see this is by converting one Spider Kitten, during a fight with other Spider Kittens.

name: Spiderling
description: Burrows inside its victims, inflicting Infested.
wikiBehavior: Spiderlings attack at melee range by burrowing into their targets, dealing 3 damage and inflicting [[status:Infested]]. This effectively "kills" them, as they disappear from the board after attacking.
wikiTrivia:
* Spiderlings are among a small subset of enemies that can be spawned as familiars directly from a spell or an item. Spiderlings summoned this way will be green.
* The Spiderling is very similar to the Spider enemy from The Binding of Isaac.

name: Spiked Cat
description: Be careful of its Thorns!
wikiBehavior: The Spiked Cat is a standard melee unit that tries to get close to an enemy so it can hit it with a melee attack, dealing 5 damage. It innately has [[status:Thorns]] as well as some [[status:Shield]].
wikiTrivia: * They use a male2 voice for cats, voiced by Matthias Bossi of Ridiculon.

name: Spookie
description: Its melee attack drains mana. Undead.
wikiBehavior:
Licks a cat, administering 5 damage and stealing all of the target's [[stat:MANA]].

It's a Flying Ghost unit, who moves via teleportation. Being body-less, it dies when downed.

It's one of two enemies that can potentially spawn when a [[obj:Tombstone (Ghost)]] is destroyed, with the other one being the Scary. This can also happen during the fight with Dybbuk, though (like Dybbuk's spawned units) they will flee if Dybbuk is defeated.
wikiTrivia:
* Despite the [[ability:Seance]] spell merely saying it summons "a ghost Familiar", it always summons a Spookie; unless the user is downed, in which case it mimics the effect of [[ability:Summon Shade]] instead.
* Its name combined with the other ghost enemy, Scary, is likely a reference to the song [[url:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sVjk5nrb_lI|"Spooky Scary Skeletons"]].
* Its appearance and behavior are similar to that of Boos in the Super Mario series, particularly in Luigi's Mansion.

name: Sprout
description: Possesses adjacent units on its turn.
wikiBehavior:
Immobile. Immune to [[status:Poison]] and el. 
On its turn puffs on all adjacent tiles, turning them to grass tiles and inflicting [[status:Possessed]]. 
Other Sprouts are immune to puff. Very likely, that other herbal enemies too. 
Does not leave a corpse. Runs if other allies are dead.

name: Spun Cat
description: Has a random class basic attack that inflicts a randomly assigned debuff.
wikiBehavior: Has different damage value depending on what class it is imitating. Has a random class basic attack that inflicts a randomly assigned debuff. Some classes of spun cat attack multiple times. The debuff does not change between attacks, if it was poison for the first attack it will be poison for all the attacks. The necromancer basic attack inflicts leech and another debuff. The druid attack still grants +1 temp damage, but the AI uses it offensively. The Tinkerer version will craft and attack with 0 Tech items.
wikiTrivia:
* The Spun Cats' name and appearance is a reference to the Spun transformation from The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth, which requires the player to collect three syringe items to attain.
* Spun Cats appear to have somehow gotten into the Lab's stash of [[item:Experimental Treatment (Head)]] and [[item:Ability Syringe]].
* If added to your party through a method such as [[item:Friendship Bracelet]], the imitated class will change between combats instead of remaining constant.

name: Squirrel
wikiBehavior: The Squirrel is a melee unit that has a multi-hit flurry that can hit 1-3 times, dealing 1 damage per hit.

name: Stacy (Enemy)
description: Its melee attack inflicts Charm. Can heal and grant All Stats Up to its allies.
wikiBehavior:
Stacy will perform a melee attack that inflicts [[status:Charmed]] on anything it contacts.
If there are no enemies in range, it will instead use that same melee attack to  heal and provide [[status:All Stats Up]] to its allies.
wikiTrivia:
* Each Stacy unit has a randomly generated six-digit number following its name. For example, "Stacy #021026".
* Her internal  name stacy2p0 (Stacy 2.0) is a reference to her being a replacement created by Dr.Beanies.

name: Steel Fly
description: Invulnerable.
wikiBehavior:
Summoned by [[item:Steel Ball]]. 
Invulnerable to conventional damage and status effects, but can still be killed by instant death enemy attacks (such as getting eaten by Daddy Shark).

name: Stegosaurus
description: Does a spin attack at the start of its turn.  Will seek grass to consume.  Will counterattack units that attack it from behind.  Trample.
wikiBehavior: Heals 5 HP when it eats tall grass. Heals 2 HP when it eats short grass.
wikiTrivia:
* Stegosaurus (Greek for "roof-lizard") was a genus of Dinosaurs around for at least 10 million years, first appearing in the fourth quarter of the Jurassic. 
** Three different Stegosaurus species are universally recognized; stenops (the one with the most complete fossil record), ungulatus (the biggest), and sulcatus.
** The purpose of their famous back plates and tail spikes is still hotly debated.

name: Stem Cat
description: Melee attacker.
wikiBehavior:
Spawns a [[url:https://mewgenics.wiki.gg/wiki/Clot/|Clot]] when damaged.
Always spawns with 2 [[status:Health Regen]].
* [[ability:Reanimate]] does not give Stem Cats their 2 [[status:Health Regen]] back.
wikiTrivia:
* If a player tries to loot the Throbbing King’s corpse while on a solo run, a Stem Cat will appear in the looting cutscene instead of the player’s other cats.
* Their namesake comes from [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_cell|stem cells]], which are undifferentiated cells with the potential to become other types of cells.

name: Strange Egg
description: What could it hatch into?
wikiBehavior:
Cannot move or attack. When it spawns will roll between 1-4 and [[status:Transformation]] after that amount of turns.
Can transform into one of the following, with equal chance:
#Y-Blaster
#G-Alien
#B-Prober
#Amoeba
#Waggle
#Moon Worm
#Korbee
#Brain Drain
#Fetus
#Fetus Gusher
wikiTrivia:
* Known in the game files as "AlienEgg"
* Its internal name and appearance are a reference to the [[url:https://avp.fandom.com/wiki/Ovomorph_(Egg)|Ovomorphs (Xenomorph eggs)]] from the Alien film series.

name: Summoned Clot
description: Has a chance to become a Clone at the end of its turn.
wikiBehavior:
* Will try to stay away from enemies
* After it moves, has a 50% chance of replacing itself with an AI controlled copy of the summoner.
** If successful, a red-colored copy with with half [[stat:HEALTH]] will spawn, and the clot will despawn.

name: T-Rex
description: Will seek out the last unit that damaged it and attempt to eat it.  Will stomp and inflict Immobile on adjacent units at the end of its turn.  Trample.
wikiBehavior:
Does not have normal attack. Insta kills units. Prioritizes killing units that damaged it. Turns and faces the direction it was damaged from.

Despite being a 2x2 unit, T-Rexes target only one tile at a time. The exception is when ending their turn; all enemies adjacent to a T-Rex are [[status:Immobile]].
wikiTrivia:
* Tyrannosaurus rex was but one species of Tyrannosaurids, albeit one of the most successful (judging by how widespread its fossils have been found).
** In real life, T. rex was only around for the very-late Cretaceous period; fossil records give it a 3-million-year range, ending a few thousand years before the end of non-avian Dinosaurs as a whole, though some theorize a range of 11 million years.
** Even with how large Cats are (or how small humans are) in Mewgenics, the T-Rexes in-game are at most half the size of real ones.
* While T. rex wasn't around for the real-life Jurassic, some of its Tyrannosauroid ancestors were.
dangerFlag: Insta-kills any unit it attacks. No way to survive the hit.

name: Tall Skeleton Cat
description: Its ranged attack can also give Shield to its allies. Will come back from the dead if its body isn't destroyed! Undead.
wikiBehavior:
The Tall Skeleton Cat is a straight-line ranged attacker that can either attack its enemies or give [[status:Shield]] to allied units with its attack. 
They have two attack actions per turn. They tend to split their attacks between shielding allies and damaging enemies, although may spend both on one option or the other depending on available targets. 
They are undead enemies, making them vulnerable to damage from Holy element spells. 
Like other skeletal enemies, when downed they won't die immediately, rather they leave a corpse behind that will revive itself if it isn't destroyed before its next turn.
wikiTrivia:
* Like most skeleton enemies, the jaw of this cat is rather made of what seems to be a curved femur bone and teeth

* This cats first appearence is in Edmund's official video of [[url:https://youtu.be/zmTtHcm7z3Y?si=lv%20M3r2NRB2Rn10i|Them kitty bones]] which included the bone yard’s song and was released 3 years before mewgenics offical release

name: Tall Tumor
description: Drains unspent mana from its enemies when they end their turn. Deals damage equal to the mana drained.  Counterattacks with a spin attack when damaged.
wikiBehavior:
Starts at half health. 
Drains mana from cats when they end their turn, and deals damage to them equal to mana drained. Heals equal to mana drained. 
Will run if they are the only enemies left.
wikiTrivia: * Due to its animations apparently crashing Adobe Animate, the Tall Tumor has its own dedicated SWF file separated from the other 4 main SWF files.
dangerFlag: Drains mana from all cats when they end their turn, dealing damage equal to mana drained.

name: Tar Baby
description: Its ranged attack creates Tar tiles.  Leaves Tar tiles in its path.
wikiBehavior:
The Tar Baby trails [[obj:Tar]] wherever it goes. It has a spit attack that does Physical Damage, applies [[status:Tarred]], and creates a [[obj:Tar]] at the targeted tile (which adds another [[status:Tarred]] if the tile was something else beforehand).

Tar Babies are instantly destroyed by el.
wikiTrivia:
* The name "Tar Baby" is a reference to "the Tar-Baby", an African-American folktale where [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Br%27er_Rabbit|Br'er Rabbit]] fights [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tar-Baby|the eponymous figure]] (actually a doll covered in tar) and unwittingly ensnares himself.
* Tar Baby's champion form is a reference to Ash from [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_End_Is_Nigh_(video_game)|The End Is Nigh]].

name: Tatters
description: Its attack inflicts Leech on all units in an area. Will inflict Hex on units that damage it. Undead.
attackStyle: Inflicts Leeches 1 on all enemies in Range
wikiBehavior: Starts with missing health. Has spread attack that inflicts [[status:Leeches]] on many enemies in an area. Inflicts [[status:Hex]] on the attacking unit when damaged.

name: Ten Tickles
description: Can attack any tile adjacent to water. Teleports through water tiles.
attackStyle: "Melee" attack Can hit any unit in or next to water
wikiBehavior: Can Teleport to any Water Tile, which doesn't trigger tile movement effects such as bear trap. Can do a melee hit on any tile adjacent to water tile. Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia: * Ten Tickles is a homophonic pun based on its phonetic similarity to the word tentacles. The phrase is typically used as the answer to the joke "How many tickles does it take to make an octopus laugh?"

name: Tesla Coil (Familiar)
wikiBehavior:
* The coil is static, and will hit random units within a distance of 3 tiles for 3 el damage with a 10% chance to [[status:Stun]].
** The random unit hit is somewhat weighed, but the priority is unknown (hardcoded).cn Cannot hit itself.
* Will attack again upon being hit.
wikiTrivia: *  Tesla Coil  is an electrical device designed by inventor Nikola Tesla. It is used to produce high voltage, low current, high frequency alternating current.

name: The Collective
description: Has a spin attack. Counterattacks when hit. Mimics the attacks and counters of all other cats in The Collective.
wikiBehavior:
* Every cat in The Collective uses a spin attack at the same time.
* Whenever any cat in The Collective is hit, all cats part of The Collective will counterattack with a melee attack in the direction the hurt cat was hit from.
dangerFlag: All cats counterattack simultaneously when any member is hit.

name: The Intruder
description: Its melee attack has Lifesteal. Will move away after it attacks. Immune to tile effects.
wikiBehavior: It is a variant of Spider Cat, different only in name and appearance.
wikiTrivia: * This is likely a reference to an item of the same name from ''The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

name: The Lost
description: Its melee attacks can inflict Fear or Doom! Undead.
wikiBehavior:
Has two different melee attacks; one inflicts [[status:Fear]], while the other inflicts [[status:Doomed]]. Neither attack does damage.

It's a Flying Ghost unit, who moves via teleportation. Being bodiless, it does not leave a corpse when downed.
wikiTrivia: * Its name and ghostly appearance is a reference to the character of the same name from The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth.

name: Throbbing Servant
description: Ranged attacker that has a chance to destroy equipment and attach a parasite. Spawns maggots.
wikiBehavior:
* Will prefer to keep distance from the player's cats.
* Has a ranged lobbed attack with 2 tile range that deals 5 damage and has a 15% chance to destroy equipment and equip the cat with a parasite from the Parasite Pool.
* Can cast a spell to spawn a [[type:Maggot]] enemy from the following list:
* # Maggot - 2/5 chance (40%)
* # Burfer Maggot - 1/5 chance (20%)
* # Chargey Maggot - 1/5 chance (20%)
* # Diggy Maggot - 1/5 chance (20%)
dangerFlag: 15% chance per hit to destroy equipment and replace it with a parasite.

name: Throbbing Turret
description: Ranged area attack that inflicts Bleed. Spawns Clots if nothing is in range.
wikiBehavior: Attacks like a turret. Immobile. Attack spawns water tiles.

name: Thump
description: Performs a jump attack. Can only be damaged from behind.
wikiBehavior:
Moves randomly. Jumps to attack, damaging and displacing all units it lands on and knocking back any adjacent units. 
Does not leave a corpse.
wikiTrivia: * Thump’s name and appearance are likely a reference to [[url:https://www.mariowiki.com/Thwomp|Thwomp]] from the Super Mario franchise. The weakspot on its back is also likely a reference to [[url:https://www.mariowiki.com/Whomp|Whomp]].

name: Tina's Friend
description: Melee Attacker. Flying.
wikiBehavior: Has a melee attack and [[status:Flying]] movement.
wikiTrivia: * The Fly's blue appearance might be a reference to the Blue Flies from The Binding of Isaac:Rebirth.

name: Tiny Tumor
description: Its melee attack causes cats it hits to lose -1 Constitution permanently and has a chance to give them cancer.
wikiBehavior:
* Tiny Tumor is a [[status:Flying]] unit, with [[status:Brace]].

* Will attempt to fly to enemies and attack them from melee range, with an attack that reduces 1 [[stat:CON]] permanently and has a 30% chance of causing [[disorder:Cancer]].
wikiTrivia:
* The game's code has an enemy version of this familiar, but it is currently unused.
** Due to how Tiny Tumors appear, they were likely meant to appear in [[chapter:The End]].
dangerFlag: Permanently reduces CON by 1. 30% chance to inflict Cancer disorder.

name: Toad
wikiBehavior:
Usually player controlled.

Has a ranged attack that pulls the first enemy hit in a line ahead of it in range 3.

name: Toadie
description: Disguises itself as inanimate objects. While disguised, ambushes enemies that walk past it, causing Fear.
attackStyle: Melee attack Inflicts Fear 1 if ambush
wikiBehavior:
On its turn, it will attempt to melee attack and then back away to disguise itself as an inanimate object. Gets revealed when Damaged or when it attacks.

When an enemy walks adjacent to a disguised Toadie, it will attack automatically, interrupting that enemy's movement and inflicting [[status:Fear]]. This drops the Toadie's disguise.

* May start battle already disguised. In that case they will not move or take turns until revealed.

* Toadies may Run if there are no non-Toadies allied with them in the current battle.
wikiTrivia: *Its appearance is similar to the rare bad outcome of the event encountered in [[chapter:The Jurassic]], which give the player’s cat the disorder [[disorder:Albinism]] and the a mutation.

name: Tom Tom
description: It's slow, but has a wide melee attack.
wikiTrivia:
* The name "Tom Tom" seems to be derived from "[[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomcat|Tomcat]]," which is a slang term for a sexually mature male cat that has not yet been neutered.
** Tomcat could also refer to the slang term of the same name, used to describe a man who is sexually promiscuous or a womanizer.
* They use a .5 pitch male1 voice for cats, voiced by Jon Evans of Ridiculon.
* Tom Toms are the only Cat-type enemy that is able to be spawned from hunter abilities. They will be tinted green if they are spawned from any action on the cat’s side.

name: Tracy (Enemy)
description: Performs a spin attack.
wikiBehavior: Performs a spin attack. She will try to counter attack with her left arm when hit.

name: Tremblo
description: Its melee attack inflicts Stun and spawns rocks.
wikiBehavior:
The Tremblo's standout feature is its ability to eat rocks; upon doing so it gains a stack of [[status:Brace]] and some [[status:Shield]]. 
The Tremblo has a suction ability to bring rocks to it, however it may also use it to damage enemies that stand between it and the rock. 
When rocks aren't available, the Tremblo will attack its enemies with a wide melee attack that inflicts knockback and has a chance to [[status:Stun]]. This attack also spawns [[obj:Rock]]. 
Does not leave a corpse.

name: Triachnid (Familiar)
wikiBehavior:
* Will attempt to take Pickups and share their effect with its summoner.
* Can spawn  allied Spiderling, up to 2 tiles away from it.
wikiTrivia:
*  Triachnid orginates from [[url:https://www.newgrounds.com/portal/view/347467||Tri-achnid]], one of Edmund McMillen's previous games.
** They also [[url:https://bindingofisaac.fandom.com/wiki/Triachnid|appeared]] in The Binding of Isaac.

name: Triceratops
description: Has a dash attack.  Counterattacks units that damage it and flings them backwards.  Trample.
wikiBehavior:
Triceratopes have a Dash attack that brings them to the edge of the map (or up to an inert obstacle), doing both its Physical Damage and its [[status:Trample]] at the same time. It requires a single turn of "ramp-up", during which their targeted tiles are highlighted. However, when attacked, Triceratopes will turn to face their attacker (changing their targeted tiles in the process).

When struck within Melee range, Triceratopes will Counterattack adjacent units in that direction; this does just their Physical Damage, but it also sends the units flying.

Each Triceratops has a 2x2 "footprint" and gets 2 turns per round.
wikiTrivia: * Triceratops (Ancient Greek for "three-horned face") was one of the last dinosaurs, around just in time for [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicxulub_crater|the asteroid]] that ended Dinosaurian supremacy. While the Triceratops was only around for three million years, there are fossils of Ceratopsian dinosaurs dated to the Jurassic.

name: Tumor Cat
description: Will dash forward 10 tiles with Trample when damaged. Blind.
wikiBehavior:
Starts with 1 [[status:Brace]]. 
Cannot attack on its own, but will try to position itself pointed at enemy for possible charge. 
When attacked, charges forward until solid obstacle, [[status:Trample]] everything on way.
wikiTips:
* Due to being harmless if not provoked, they can be ignored in favor of more apparent threats.
* Tumor Cats are not immune to fire, and therefore, can be tricked into dashing through large pools of [[obj:Lava]], giving them large stacks of [[status:Burn]].

name: Tumorhead
description: Its melee attack knocks units back 3 tiles. Dashes forward when damaged.
wikiBehavior:
Starts with 1 [[status:Brace]]. 
When damaged, propels itself forward like a Gassy but without a poison.
wikiTrivia: * Tumorheads are seen in the cutscene that pops up when The Core is unlocked.

name: Turkey
description: Whoever kills this gets All Stats Up and finds a bonus item!
wikiBehavior:
Turkeys are peaceful enemies with a low chance of appearing when the player enters the level. 

Their turns consist of moving to random tiles, they do not interact with other units by themselves. When moving, they ignore hazards such as brambles. 

Like all Large Birds, it will run away after 3 turns. 

When hit, it attempts to attack whoever damaged it with a melee attack, then moves away. 

If killed prior to flying out, whoever kills it gains an [[status:All Stats Up]] and finds a bonus at the end of combat.
wikiTrivia:
* [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey_(bird)|Turkeys]] are relatively-large birds of the order Galliformes, which also contains Chickens.
* For unknown reasons, the attack animation for the Turkey (and the other 3 large bonus birds) uses an open, black beak for a few frames in its attack animation.

name: Turret
wikiBehavior: Cannot move, uses a lobbed attack within 6 tile range.

name: Turtle
wikiBehavior:
Has an attack with range 2 and knockback that moves the turtle forward one tile.
* This attack is identical to the [[class:Tank]]'s default basic attack, [[ability:Push Attack]]
wikiTrivia:
* The Turtle’s champion form is a reference to the  Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.
* Despite the Turtle’s name, it actually appears to be a tortoise.
* Internally, The Turtle is considered to be a type of Dog.
** This may be a reference to Elden Ring and it's playerbase. Players would keep leaving messages describing various animals (Notably, Turtles) as "dogs" throughout the game world.

name: Twister
description: Moves towards its enemies. Tosses what it touches.
wikiBehavior:
* Moves 2 tiles towards its enemies every turn.
* Twisters have very high initiative (10000) meaning they will almost always move first in the round.
* When a Twister touches a unit, the unit will be tossed 3-5 tiles away and take 5 damage.
* Twisters have [[status:Flying]] and phasing, meaning they can move through any tile without getting hit. They are also Inanimate, meaning they can't take damage from attacks.
* All Twisters start with a hidden [[status:Doomed]] passive, meaning they will die after 2 rounds.
* Will reflect all projectiles thrown into it.
dangerFlag: Inanimate and immune to all damage and status effects. Tosses units 3-5 tiles for 5 damage. Moves first every round.

name: Übercat
description: Has a leap attack that does knockback in an area.   Reflects projectiles. Uncapped HP.
wikiBehavior: Has [[status:Trample]]. Bounces back units that contact it 2 tiles. Uses a leap attack called Lasagnefloppen that damages and knocks back surrounding units.
wikiTrivia:
* Übercat bears a striking resemblance to Garfield, albeit with a missing nose.
** The "Lasagnefloppen" attack references Garfield's favorite food.
** Garfield is known to be fat and lazy, making him similar to the other Über-units (Überman and Überwoman).
** The Level editor sprite for Übercat is a poorly-drawn depiction of Garfield himself.

name: Überman
description: Melee attacker with Knockback.
wikiBehavior:
* Moves slowly towards the player's cats with [[status:Trample]]. Bounces back attackers and projectiles. Inflicts [[status:Bruise]] on hit units.
* Their bodies block movement even after death.
wikiTrivia:
* Known internally as "Fat Man".
* Their appearance may be a reference to the movie [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WALL-E|Wall-E]]. In it, the humans of the future lose the ability to move without hover chairs as a result of becoming morbidly obese.
* Their name is a reference to the [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%9Cbermensch|Übermensch]].

name: Überwoman
description: Melee attacker with Knockback.
wikiTrivia:
* It is known internally as "Fat Woman"
* Their appearance may be a reference to the movie [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WALL-E|Wall-E]]. In it the people of the future lose the ability to move without hover chairs.
* Their champion version’s hair may be a reference to Isaac's Mom from The Binding of Isaac.

name: Waggle
description: Melee attacker.  Will turn enemy familiars and low health allies into Waggles!
wikiBehavior:
* Uses a melee attack. 
* Instead of killing units they can kill in one hit, they typically transform them into allied Waggles, with full [[stat:HEALTH]] (7 or 14). Waggles transformed from larger units will retain the larger size, allowing 2x2 and 3x3 Waggles to be created. 2x2 Waggles have the same description as 1x1 Waggles, while 3x3 Waggles have the description "HOLY FUCKING SHIT".
** Currently, the only way to get a 3x3 Waggle is to use [[ability:Eternal Servitude]] on the Crater Maker.
** This affects familiars and allied units, but not other Waggles.
** Units transformed by Champion Waggles will always transform into Champion Waggles as well.
* Does not leave a corpse.
dangerFlag: Transforms units it can one-shot into allied Waggles instead of killing them.

name: Water Kitten
description: Moves away when damaged. May be hiding in water...
wikiBehavior:
* Creates water tiles when moving.
* Can either spawn in combat normally or be hidden in water tiles, emerging into combat if a cat or familiar comes within two tiles.
* Has normal Kitten behavior, running away when damaged.

name: Water Leech
description: Seeks water when its out of water. While in water, dashes in a straight line with Lifesteal that passes through units.
attackStyle: Piercing dash attack, Infinite Range Lifesteal
wikiBehavior:
Its speed is reduced to 3 when not on a [[obj:Water]]. 
Only while in water, it can perform a Dash attack with [[status:Lifesteal]]. This attack deals 4 physical damage, scales with [[stat:STR]] and ignores [[status:Shield]]. 
The dash attack will continue through units until it hits a wall or inanimate object.
While on land it can't attack and will attempt to return to water.

name: Werecat
description: Can use both its dash attack and its leap attack in the same turn.
attackStyle: Dash attack, Range 2 Leap attack, Range ?, Blindspot
wikiBehavior:
* Will "bark" 3 times at the start of the battle, indicating their presence.
* Has two separate movement actions and two different attack actions: charge and jump that knocks back anything next to target tile. They can do all of this in single turn.
wikiTrivia:
* Werecats are a play on the concept of werewolves, which are individuals who can shapeshift into a wolf-like creature.
** Within the context of the game, it is not clear whether the Werecat is meant to be a cat that has shifted into a wolf-like creature or a man that has shifted into a cat-like creature, though based on the existence of a similar Wereman enemy, and the fact that they "bark" at the beginning of the battle, it is likely the former.

name: Wereman
description: Has a multi-hit melee attack.
wikiBehavior:
Will spawn from Caveman Men or Caveman Women being attacked by a Sabertooth Cat or Sabertooth Kitten. Hates Cavemen!
Its multi hit melee attack has cleave. The final hit of its multi hit melee attack has knock up 3.
wikiTrivia: * Although the Wereman's name was possibly given to differentiate it from the already similarly named Werecat (both of which are a play on the concept of werewolves), the name of this enemy as derived from Old English would literally be 'man-man'.

name: Whisperer
description: "Its ranged attack inflicts Bruise and -2 Speed to enemies, and Brace and +2 Speed to allies. Its melee attack inflicts charm."
wikiBehavior:
Has an allegiance-sensitive ranged attack "Tumor throw" with targeting radius of 3. 
If used on ally, will heal it and inflict 2 [[status:Brace]] and +2 [[stat:SPD]]. 
If used on enemy, will damage it and inflict 2 [[status:Bruise]] and -2 [[stat:SPD]]. 
Its melee move "Whisper" inflicts [[status:Charmed]].

name: Wisp
description: Its melee attack inflicts Burn. Dodges one attack per turn.
wikiBehavior:
Uses a low damage melee attack that inflicts [[status:Burn]] 2. 
Guaranteed to dodge one instance of damage each round, if it would otherwise hit them. 
* This is visualized by the fire around their body; it goes out when they dodge something.
* A dodge is different from a block, in that knockback doesn't apply.
Does not leave a corpse when killed and permanently has [[status:Flying]].
wikiTrivia: * They resemble the [[url:https://thelegendofbumbo.fandom.com/wiki/Whisp|Whisp]] enemies from The Legend of Bum-Bo.

name: Wooly Mammoth
description: Has a melee attack that knocks units into the air, and a dash attack. Will bruise and Knockback adjacent units at the start of its turn. Trample
wikiBehavior: Creates dirt tiles below it. Counts as a cat, as evidenced by caveman men attacking it.

name: Y-Blaster
description: "Shoots at units that cross its path. Gains +1 Damage at the end of its turn. Moves away when in danger."
wikiBehavior: Moving to, or past, any tile perpendicular to Y-Blaster causes it to shoot a piercing lazer in that direction, hitting allies and enemies. Moves away when your cats move into one of its 4 adjacent tiles.
wikiTrivia:
* Y-Blasters are potentially a reference to [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Behemoth|The Behemoth's]] 2002 game [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alien_Hominid|Alien Hominid]], which features a yellow alien with a green blaster. 
** This is most likely a nod to the co-founder of The Behemoth, [[url:https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Fulp|Tom Fulp]] (creator of Newgrounds) who [[url:https://www.thegeekgeneration.com/2020/04/edmund-mcmillen-interview-tapeworm-and-the-binding-of-isaac/|promoted]] and [[url:https://www.newgrounds.com/portal/view/435703|sponsored]] Edmund McMillen early in his career, and [[url:https://www.newgrounds.com/portal/view/358510|helped him]] with the prototype for [[url:https://www.newgrounds.com/portal/view/358510|Cereus Peashy]] ([[url:https://gameinformer.com/2021/12/27/the-outcast-comes-home-the-life-and-career-of-edmund-mcmillen|extra source]]).
** Additionally, Alien Hominid appears in Super Meat Boy.
* Its internal nickname is "yellow blaster", most likely being its full name.
* A Champion Y-Blaster is one of the background cameos on the map of the Moon.

name: Yeti
description: Has a triple-hit melee attack and a close-range Freeze attack.
wikiBehavior: Has a triple hit melee attack that inflicts bleed. Has a 3-range conical [[status:Freeze]] attack. One of its attacks has knock back.

name: Yeti Cat
description: Its ranged ice attack inflicts Slow and has a chance to inflict Freeze. Counter attacks melee attackers.
wikiBehavior: Counter attacks melee attackers. Its counter attack can freeze. Has ranged ice attack that inflicts slow and has a chance to freeze and can only hit units exactly 2 tiles away.

name: Zombie Cat
description: Eats corpses and becomes stronger! Taking damage weakens it and spawns poison food. Undead.
wikiBehavior:
Zombie Cats behave similarly to cats with [[disorder:Necrosis]]. When hit, they drop a Pickup and receive Stat-Down Debuffs in [[stat:STR]] and [[stat:CON]].

Zombie Cats will prioritize using their Feast ability. This allows them to feed on an adjacent downed unit, giving them +3 [[stat:STR]] and +2 [[stat:CON]], an extra turn, and healing for 8 [[stat:HEALTH]].
wikiTrivia: * The Zombie Cats' droopy right eyes may be a reference to the Zombie Dogs in the Dragon Quest series, such as the [[url:https://dragon-quest.org/w/index.php?title=Putrefido|Putrefido]].

name: Zombie Kitten
wikiBehavior: Much like their Zombie Cat successors, Zombie Kittens will prioritize using their Feast ability on downed units. They gain [[status:Strength Up]], [[status:Constitution Up]], and Heal. This attack will destroy the corpse.
